43 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 13 standard (1 credit), 10 advanced (5), 1 premium (10), 19 custom (flat/metered) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

## GET /v1/instagram/audio/reels - 1 credit (standard)

Returns reels that use a specific audio track on Instagram. Each reel includes engagement metrics and author info. The `audio_id` is the `post.ext.music_id` a reel carries on /v1/instagram/post and /v1/instagram/profile/reels, or on /v1/instagram/profile/posts with include=audio, so reels that share a sound can be expanded into every other reel using it. On the first page `data.total` is the number of reels Instagram shows for the sound, or null when that count is not available, and later pages leave it null. On the first page `data.is_trending` is `true` when Instagram currently marks the sound as trending in Reels and `false` when it does not; it changes over time, later pages leave it null, and it is null when that signal is not available. On the first page `data.sound` describes the sound itself as `{ track_title, artist, is_original, creator_username, created_at, duration_seconds, is_explicit, spotify_track_id, first_reel_url }`: on an original sound `creator_username` is the account that created it, `created_at` is when it was created and `first_reel_url` is the reel it was first used on, while on a licensed track those three are null and `spotify_track_id` is filled when Instagram links the track to Spotify; `data.sound` is null on later pages and when the sound's details are not available. When `audio_id` is a cluster id, `data.total` counts every upload in the cluster and `data.sound` describes the one upload Instagram shows for it, so its creator is not necessarily the cluster's first user. To record `data.total` every day, create a Monitor that tracks `total`; see /docs/recipes/track-sound-growth. Each reel carries `post.ext.audio_cluster_id`, Instagram's audio cluster for that reel: the id Instagram uses to group different uploads of the same sound. It is absent on a reel when it is not available. A page carries up to about 12 reels, in the order Instagram's own audio page lists them, which is not by date. Pass `pagination.next_cursor` back as `cursor` to request the next page. A page that comes back empty is not charged. On a reel also posted to Facebook, `engagement.views` can include its Facebook views: `post.ext.instagram_views` is the Instagram-only figure, the same on every Instagram endpoint, and `post.ext.facebook_views` is the Facebook part when the source reports it.

**Use when** Use it after search/music or music/trending: pass the audio_id to see who is posting with that sound.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** cursor · ≈12/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/12) x 1 credits · typical 2.5-4.5 s

**Query params**

- `audio_id` (required) - Instagram audio ID: the numeric id from an instagram.com/reels/audio/{audio_id}/ URL · e.g. `1392969992841787`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response to fetch the next page.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+15 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, views}; `post.flags` {deleted, pinned}. Also in the sample: `post.ext` {media_type string, audio_cluster_id string, published_at_epoch number, coauthors array} (+5 more). Never filled: `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.is_trending`, `data.sound`.

**Next** `instagram/post/stats` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post stats including the share count.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/audio/reels" \
  --data-urlencode "audio_id=1392969992841787" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/basic-profile - 1 credit (standard)

Returns basic public profile info for an Instagram user by user ID including username, full name, bio, avatar, verification status, and the follower, following and lifetime post counts.

**Use when** all you have is a numeric user id and only need the name and avatar; use profile for bio, follower counts, and verification.
**Cost** cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `userId` (optional, string) - Instagram numeric user ID · e.g. `314216`

| Field | Meaning |

| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+12 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, posts_count, verified, private}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `author.ext` {business_category, hd_avatar_url}. Never filled: `author.likes_count`.

**Next** `instagram/following` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - List Instagram following. · `instagram/profile/about` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - Get Instagram account transparency details.

```bash
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/comment - 5-15 credits (request-shaped)

Resolves a single Instagram comment to a live comment object (current like count, reply count, author, timestamp) without you paginating the comment section. Pass `comment_url` (an `https://www.instagram.com/p/{shortcode}/c/{commentId}/` permalink: reply permalinks `.../c/{parent}/r/{reply}/` are best-effort) OR `post_url` + `comment_id`. Instead of a comment id you can search the comment section: `author_username` or `text_contains` return up to `max` matches under `data.matches` (a search that matches nothing returns 404 and is fully refunded). The response includes `lookup.post_comment_count` (the post's true total, so you can reason about scan coverage) and a `lookup.position_hint`: pass it back on a later lookup to make the re-check faster (the price is the same). Instagram does not expose pinned status or full reply threads to any provider, so `flags.pinned` stays null and deep reply lookups can return `reply_not_resolvable`. Flat 5 credits (15 with `deep_scan=true`); a not-found returns 404 and is fully refunded.

**Use when** you already know which comment you want, so you do not have to page through post/comments to find it again.
**Cost** price moves with `deep_scan` · cache 300 s
**Pricing** 5 credits for a standard lookup, 15 with `deep_scan=true`, which keeps paging the thread when the comment is not in the first pages. Reach for deep_scan only after a standard lookup comes back not-found.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `comment_url` (optional, string) - An Instagram comment permalink: `https://www.instagram.com/p/{shortcode}/c/{commentId}/` (or a reply permalink `.../c/{parent}/r/{reply}/`, best-effort). Mutually exclusive with `post_url`+`comment_id`. · e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/p/CnpPou9hWqq/c/18007013966365752/`
- `post_url` (optional, string) - The post URL (a `/p/`, `/reel/`, `/reels/`, or `/tv/` link; an app share link `instagram.com/share/...` works too). Combine with `comment_id`, or with `author_username`/`text_contains` for a search.
- `comment_id` (optional, string) - The target comment's numeric id (`pk`). Requires `post_url`.
- `author_username` (optional, string) - Return up to `max` comments authored by this username (no comment id needed). Mutually exclusive with `text_contains` and any comment id.
- `text_contains` (optional, string) - Return up to `max` comments whose text contains this snippet (case-insensitive). Mutually exclusive with `author_username` and any comment id.
- `deep_scan` (optional, boolean) - Widen the scan budget for deeply-buried comments (raises the per-chain page ceiling and deadline). Bills 15 credits instead of 5.
- `position_hint` (optional, string) - Opaque token from a prior lookup's `lookup.position_hint`. Passing it back replays just the last-known sort chain first, making a re-check of an already-found comment cheap.
- `max` (optional, integer) - For `author_username`/`text_contains` search: max matches to return (1-20, default 5).

**Response** `Comment` object at `data`, `{ comment, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/Comment.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `comment.text` | Comment body. |
| `comment.id` | Platform-specific comment ID (always a string) |
| `comment.published_at` | Comment creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `comment.url` | Direct URL to the comment on the source platform |
| `comment.author.username` | Comment author username (null when tombstoned) |
| `comment.parent_id` | Parent comment ID for nested replies, or null for… |

+9 more (types in the full schema): `comment` {post_id}; `comment.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `comment.engagement` {likes, replies}; `comment.flags` {deleted, pinned}; `computed` {language}. Also in the sample: `comment.ext.lookup` {found_via string, pages_fetched number, comments_scanned number, sort_basis string, position_hint string, post_comment_count number}; `lookup` {found_via string, pages_fetched number, comments_scanned number, sort_basis string} (+2 more).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/comment" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/comment/likers - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the accounts that liked one Instagram comment, each with username, display name, avatar URL, verification status and profile URL. Pass the comment's numeric id as `comment_id` (the `comment.id` on /v1/instagram/post/comments rows), or its permalink (`https://www.instagram.com/p/{shortcode}/c/{comment_id}/`) as `url`. A page carries up to about 50 accounts; pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. A comment with no likes returns an empty list, which is not charged. There is no total like count here: read `comment.engagement.likes` on the comment itself.

**Use when** you want to see who liked a specific comment. For the likers of a post, use /v1/instagram/post/likers.
**Cost** cache 300 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 1.4-2.0 s

**Query params**

- `comment_id` (optional, string) - Numeric id of the Instagram comment. · e.g. `18133095883781285`
- `url` (optional, string) - Permalink of the comment: https://www.instagram.com/p/{shortcode}/c/{comment_id}/ (a reply permalink names the reply).
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response to fetch the next page.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `comment_id`, `url`.

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |
| `author.verified` | Whether the account is verified |

Never filled: `author.bio`, `author.followers`, `author.following`, `author.likes_count`, `author.posts_count`. Page-level: `data.dropped`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/comment/likers" \
  --data-urlencode "comment_id=18133095883781285" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/engagement - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns computed engagement statistics for an Instagram account based on its recent posts: an overall engagement rate, follower count, total likes and comments across the sampled posts, and a per-post breakdown with likes, comments, post time, and likes/comments-per-hour velocity. Pass the account `handle`.

**Use when** you want the engagement math done for you, including likes and comments per hour on each post, rather than raw posts to total yourself.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - Instagram username without the @ symbol. · e.g. `mrbeast`

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {engagement_rate_percentages number, recent_posts number, followers number, comments number, likes number, recent_posts_explanation string, id_user string, username string, is_private boolean}; `posts_details[]` {likes number, comments number, taken_at number, datetime string, hours_since_post number, time_ago string, likes_per_hour number, comments_per_hour number}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/engagement" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=mrbeast" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/followers - 5-10 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a paginated list of the accounts that follow an Instagram user. Each follower includes username, display name, avatar URL, verification status, and profile URL. Pass either `handle` or `user_id`, and page through with `cursor`. A public account with no followers returns 200 with an empty list and `data.total` 0, not an error, and is not charged. A plain walk can end before the profile's count: on most accounts it ends within a few rows of that count, and on large verified accounts Instagram caps every route at about 50 rows with no cursor, so a plain walk ends there. `data.total` carries the profile's own count on every page, so compare the rows you collected against it. Send `coverage=full` with `handle` to walk a merged list instead: each page is drawn from several reads of the list and carries no account twice inside a page, until the rows reach the count or no read has more. Across consecutive pages a handful of accounts can repeat on the pages one source covered on its own; the merged walk, which never returns an account it has already given you, runs wherever that source cannot cover the list. A full-coverage page costs 10 credits instead of 5 and takes longer, and its cursor only continues a `coverage=full` walk. Send `query` to search inside the list instead of paging it: one window of the accounts in the list whose username or display name contains the query, so the exact username of an account tells you whether it is on the list. An empty list means no account in the list matches. A `query` call has no cursor and no `data.total`, and it cannot be combined with `cursor` or `coverage=full`. On large verified accounts Instagram limits the list and does not search it, so the search runs on the roughly 50 accounts Instagram shows, only the ones that match are returned, and `data._warnings` says so: an account the answer does not return may still be on the list.

**Use when** you want to walk an account's follower list, passing either handle or user_id and paging deeper with the cursor it returns.
**Cost** price moves with `coverage` · cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits a page. Up to three reads are merged into one page, typically about 50 accounts, and a page can carry fewer. With `coverage=full`, up to 10 credits a page, settled down to 5 when the plain walk covered the whole page. A page that fails is refunded. With `query`, 5 credits for its one window, and nothing when no account matches.
**Paging** cursor · 50/page · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/50) x 5-10 credits · typical 3.8-7.2 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username without the @ symbol. · e.g. `mrbeast`
- `user_id` (optional, string) - Instagram numeric user ID. Use this for faster responses.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response to fetch the next page.
- `coverage` (optional, enum: full) - Send `full` to walk a merged list: accounts are added from several reads of the list and no account appears twice inside a page, until the rows reach the profile's count in `data.total`. On the pages one source covered on its own a handful of accounts can repeat across consecutive pages; wherever that source cannot cover the list the merged walk runs instead, and it never returns an account it has already given you. Requires `handle`. 10 credits a page instead of 5, settled down to 5 on any page a single read covered in full. Up to three reads are merged into one page, typically about 50 accounts, so a full list costs at most roughly the account count divided by 50, times 10 credits: on 13/09/2026 a following list of 2,652 took 54 pages and a follower list of 2,360 took 59, because the later pages of a follower walk add fewer new accounts. A page usually takes about 8 seconds and can take up to about 45, and a `503` is retried with the same cursor. A cursor from this mode only continues this mode.
- `query` (optional, string) - A username or name to look for in the list. Returns the accounts whose username or display name contains it (ignoring case and accents) in one window with no cursor, at the price of a page, and nothing is charged when no account matches. Cannot be combined with `cursor` or `coverage`.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `handle`, `user_id`.

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |
| `author.verified` | Whether the account is verified |

Never filled: `author.bio`, `author.followers`, `author.following`, `author.likes_count`, `author.posts_count`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.truncated`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/followers" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=mrbeast" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/following - 5-10 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a paginated list of the accounts an Instagram user follows. Each account includes username, display name, avatar URL, verification status, and profile URL. Pass either `handle` or `user_id`, and page through with `cursor`. A public account that follows nobody returns 200 with an empty list and `data.total` 0, not an error, and is not charged. A plain walk can end before the profile's following count: on most accounts it ends within a few rows of that count, and on large verified accounts Instagram caps every route at about 50 rows with no cursor, so a plain walk ends there. `data.total` carries the profile's own count on every page, so compare the rows you collected against it. Send `coverage=full` with `handle` to walk a merged list instead: each page is drawn from several reads of the list and carries no account twice inside a page, until the rows reach the count or no read has more. Across consecutive pages a handful of accounts can repeat on the pages one source covered on its own; the merged walk, which never returns an account it has already given you, runs wherever that source cannot cover the list. A full-coverage page costs 10 credits instead of 5 and takes longer, and its cursor only continues a `coverage=full` walk. Send `query` to search inside the list instead of paging it: one window of the accounts in the list whose username or display name contains the query, so the exact username of an account tells you whether it is on the list. An empty list means no account in the list matches. A `query` call has no cursor and no `data.total`, and it cannot be combined with `cursor` or `coverage=full`. On large verified accounts Instagram limits the list and does not search it, so the search runs on the roughly 50 accounts Instagram shows, only the ones that match are returned, and `data._warnings` says so: an account the answer does not return may still be on the list.

**Use when** you want it for the other side of the graph from followers: the accounts this user chose to follow.
**Cost** price moves with `coverage` · cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits a page. Up to three reads are merged into one page, typically about 50 accounts, and a page can carry fewer. With `coverage=full`, up to 10 credits a page, settled down to 5 when the plain walk covered the whole page. A page that fails is refunded. With `query`, 5 credits for its one window, and nothing when no account matches.
**Paging** cursor · 50/page · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/50) x 5-10 credits · typical 2.6-5.9 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username without the @ symbol. · e.g. `mrbeast`
- `user_id` (optional, string) - Instagram numeric user ID. Use this for faster responses.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response to fetch the next page.
- `coverage` (optional, enum: full) - Send `full` to walk a merged list: accounts are added from several reads of the list and no account appears twice inside a page, until the rows reach the profile's count in `data.total`. On the pages one source covered on its own a handful of accounts can repeat across consecutive pages; wherever that source cannot cover the list the merged walk runs instead, and it never returns an account it has already given you. Requires `handle`. 10 credits a page instead of 5, settled down to 5 on any page a single read covered in full. Up to three reads are merged into one page, typically about 50 accounts, so a full list costs at most roughly the account count divided by 50, times 10 credits: on 13/09/2026 a following list of 2,652 took 54 pages and a follower list of 2,360 took 59, because the later pages of a follower walk add fewer new accounts. A page usually takes about 8 seconds and can take up to about 45, and a `503` is retried with the same cursor. A cursor from this mode only continues this mode.
- `query` (optional, string) - A username or name to look for in the list. Returns the accounts whose username or display name contains it (ignoring case and accents) in one window with no cursor, at the price of a page, and nothing is charged when no account matches. Cannot be combined with `cursor` or `coverage`.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `handle`, `user_id`.

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |
| `author.verified` | Whether the account is verified |

Never filled: `author.bio`, `author.followers`, `author.following`, `author.likes_count`, `author.posts_count`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.truncated`.

**Next** `instagram/profile` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - Get Instagram user profile.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/following" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=mrbeast" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/hashtag - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Instagram's own record for a hashtag: its id (`post.id`), its name (`post.content.text`), its explore page (`post.url`) and the exact number of public posts Instagram counts under it (`post.ext.posts_count`). The count is live and moves between calls minutes apart. Pass the tag with or without the leading `#`; it is matched exactly and case-insensitively, never to a similar tag, and a tag with spaces is refused free. A tag Instagram does not know returns 404 and is not charged. A hashtag has no author, media or engagement, so those leaves are null. Use /v1/instagram/search/hashtag to read the posts themselves.

**Use when** you want to size a hashtag before you collect it. Use /v1/instagram/search/hashtag to read what is under the tag.

## GET /v1/instagram/highlight/detail - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the items within a specific Instagram story highlight including media URLs, thumbnails, durations, and capture timestamps. Highlights are archived story frames, so they carry no public caption and no public like, comment, or view count. Instagram shows story engagement only to the account owner, and it is never fabricated here.

**Use when** Use it after highlights: pass the id it returned to see the contents of a single collection.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `id` (optional, string) - Instagram highlight ID: the numeric id, with or without the `highlight:` prefix. Get it from `/v1/instagram/highlights`. · e.g. `18067016518767507`
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).

| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

## GET /v1/instagram/location/posts - 5-68 credits (request-shaped)

Returns the posts tagged at an Instagram location, newest first, about 60 per page. Each post includes shortcode, URL, caption, media URLs, engagement counts, and the author. Pass `location_id` as `location.pk` from /v1/instagram/search/location, then page back in time with `cursor` until `has_more` is false. If the source that served page 1 fails on a later page, a backup source continues the walk and the page carries `continuation_rescued` in `data._warnings`: a few posts nearest the page boundary can be missing from that page. A busy place fills a page in about a day and a quiet one covers months or years, and the grid goes back to the location's oldest posts. Instagram orders the grid by when each post was created, so a scheduled post that went live later sits among older posts while its published_at shows the real publish time (about 1 post in 75, up to 13 days apart, measured 13/09/2026). To collect a time window, keep paging until a whole page is older than the window's start and filter on published_at; do not stop at the first older post. Each page is a separate call at the listed price. A location grid mixes photos and reels, so engagement.views is a number on the video rows and null on the photo rows. This is the region-scoped Instagram route: /v1/instagram/reels/trending and /v1/instagram/music/trending take no region, because Instagram ties both to the account viewing them. Note: post.author.display_name is not available on this endpoint, because the Instagram surface behind it withholds creator display names. Join on post.author.username, or pass it to /v1/instagram/profile?handle= for the name.

**Use when** Use it after search/location for region-scoped posts. Page back in time with the cursor; for a time window, stop once a whole page is older than its start.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits per page. `include=country` holds 63 more credits a page and keeps 1 per creator whose declared country came back, refunding a creator who publishes none or cannot be found, so a page with it costs 5 to 68. A page that fails is refunded in full and looks no creator up.
**Paging** cursor · ≈63/page (observed once) · depth unknown · price per N items not proven · typical 6.7-10 s

**Query params**

- `location_id` (required) - Instagram location id. Use location.pk from /v1/instagram/search/location. · e.g. `331004901`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response to fetch the next, older page.
- `safe_url` (optional, boolean) - When true, returns URL-safe media links suitable for embedding.
- `include` (optional, enum: country) - Send `country` to add each post's creator country as `post.ext.author_country`: the country the creator declares on Instagram's About this account panel, not the place the post is tagged at, and null when the creator publishes none. Every row carries the creator's numeric id as `post.ext.author_id`, which is what it is read by. 1 extra credit per creator whose country came back; two posts by one creator cost one lookup, a creator looked up in the last 30 days is free, and a creator who publishes none or cannot be found is refunded. A typo is a free 400.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.url` | 100% | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | 83% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to author profile picture |

+16 more (types in the full schema): `post.author` {verified}; `post.content` {media_urls, duration_seconds, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, views}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.ext` {author_country, author_id}; `post.flags` {deleted, pinned}. Also in the sample: `post.ext` {media_type string, carousel_count number, published_at_epoch number} (+1 more). Never filled: `post.author.display_name`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.hydration`.

**Next** `instagram/media/screen-text` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post on-screen text. · `instagram/post/stats` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post stats including the share count. · `prism/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Every comment on a post, replies nested, server-paginated to completion.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/location/posts" \
  --data-urlencode "location_id=331004901" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/media/screen-text - 5-10 credits (request-shaped)

Reads the text shown on an Instagram post: the headlines, list items, place names, captions and meme text creators design into a photo, a carousel slide or a reel, which the post caption never carries. What is read depends on the post. On a photo, the photo itself. On a carousel, every slide in order, 10 slides a call: the first 10 by default, and the next 10 with `slide_offset=10`; a longer carousel's response carries a warning giving its full slide count, and `next_slide_offset` names the offset that reads the rest (null when every slide has been read). On a reel or video, the cover frame by default, so it does not read text that appears only later in the video; with `frames=all` the whole video is read instead, up to 3 minutes (180 seconds), and the response adds `subtitles` (on-screen captions of the speech, kept apart from `texts`), a `timeline` of every text block with `at_seconds`, the second it first appears, and `kind` (text or subtitle), and `duration_seconds`. This is AI OCR of the published media. On a reel whose text was typed in Instagram's own editor, that text is also read from the post's data, exactly as typed and for every moment of the reel, and returned in `native_texts` (null when the reel has none; text added in another app is only in the pixels). `texts` is the deduplicated union of every image's text in slide order, `images` lists each image read with its own `texts` and its 0-based `index` in the post's media list (so a carousel caller knows which slide said what), `media_type` is image, video or carousel, and `source` says which layers produced text: native, native+ocr, ocr or none. A post with no text on it returns empty arrays (that is a real answer, not an error). If some slides cannot be read, those slides carry `texts: null` and the response carries a warning.

**Use when** you want it for text designed into a post, like carousel headlines; the caption lives on post and spoken words on media/transcript. Text shown later in a reel is not read.
**Cost** price moves with `frames` · cache 600 s
**Pricing** 5 credits a call, the same for a photo, a reel's cover or a carousel page of 10 slides. 10 credits with `frames=all` on a reel; when the post has no video to read, or the video cannot be read and the cover is read instead, the call costs 5 and the response says so in `warnings`. Refunded when the post cannot be found, when nothing on it could be read, or when a parameter does not fit the post (a `slide_offset` past the last slide, a reel over 180 seconds with `frames=all`).
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the Instagram post, reel or video (a `/p/`, `/reel/`, `/reels/` or `/tv/` link). A share link copied from the app (`instagram.com/share/...`) works too; a share link to a profile is refused at no charge with the handle to send, and a dead one is a free 404. · e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/p/DdEqEl5Dl-S/`
- `frames` (optional, enum: cover | all) - What to read on a reel or video. `cover` (the default) reads the cover frame for 5 credits. `all` reads the whole video, up to 180 seconds, for 10 credits, and adds `subtitles`, `timeline` and `duration_seconds`. Has no effect on photos and carousels, which are read as usual for 5 credits.
- `slide_offset` (optional, integer, min 0) - Carousels only: the 0-based index of the first slide to read, 10 slides a call. Default 0. `slide_offset=10` reads slides 11 to 20. Each image in `images` keeps its index in the whole carousel, and `next_slide_offset` gives the value for the next call.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {post_id string, shortcode string, url string, media_type string, texts string[], source string, frame null, slide_count number, warnings string[]}; `images[]` {index number, image_url string, texts string[]|array}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/media/screen-text" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DdEqEl5Dl-S/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/media/transcript - 10 credits (premium)

Returns an AI-generated transcript of the spoken words in an Instagram video or reel. The audio itself is transcribed; when that cannot be done, the captions Instagram generates for some videos are used instead, as the same plain text. A video with music, sound effects or on-screen text but no speech has nothing to transcribe. Videos up to 10 minutes (600 seconds) are supported. Every outcome below is deterministic for a given URL, so retrying returns the same answer, and none of them costs credits. A video with no speech returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND with `error.details.reason: no_speech` (the video exists). A photo post, a carousel of photos, or a URL that no longer resolves returns 404 with `reason: no_video_or_gone`, because Instagram answers those identically. A video longer than 10 minutes returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST with `error.details.reason: video_too_long`, `duration_seconds` and `max_seconds`, and a message giving its length. A video over 2 minutes is transcribed on demand and can take a minute or more, so allow up to 300 seconds before your HTTP client times out.

**Use when** you need what was said in a video rather than its metrics; pass the reel or video URL. Photo posts and videos over 10 minutes cannot be transcribed.
**Cost** cache 2592000 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the Instagram video or reel (a `/reel/`, `/p/` or `/tv/` link to a video post). Photo posts have no audio to transcribe. A share link copied from the app (`instagram.com/share/...`) works too; a share link to a profile is refused at no charge with the handle to send, and a dead one is a free 404. · e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/reel/DHsD6HGqJhp/`

**Response** `Transcript` object at `data`, `{ transcripts }` (inferred from a sample): `transcripts[]` {id string, shortcode string, text string}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/media/transcript" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.instagram.com/reel/DHsD6HGqJhp/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/music/trending - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns a chart of licensed audio tracks trending on Instagram. Each track includes its title, artist, audio and cover-artwork URLs, and usage metadata: useful for spotting sounds to ride for reach. Takes no parameters, and there is no region or country option: Instagram builds this chart for the account viewing it, so the chart reflects that account's market and cannot be selected. Every response carries `data.fetched_at`, the time the chart was read from Instagram, and `data.stale`: `false` when it was read on this call, `true` when Instagram showed only its royalty-free sound library on this call and the most recent chart read in the last 6 hours is returned instead (the chart moves slowly; check `fetched_at` if you need it fresher). When no chart has been read in the last 6 hours either, the call returns 503 and your credits are refunded; retry after a minute. For region-scoped Instagram data, use /v1/instagram/search/location and /v1/instagram/location/posts. A fresh read can take 20 to 40 seconds, so allow at least 50 seconds before timing out.

**Use when** you want to spot sounds worth posting with. It takes no region: the chart follows the viewing account's market. A 503 is refunded, so retry.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Response** `SearchResult`. Fields not published yet - call it once; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=instagram/music/trending` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/music/trending" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/post - 1 credit (standard)

Returns detailed information about a specific Instagram post including view count on videos and reels, like count, comment count, caption, media URLs, media type, author info, and tagged users. The place the post is tagged at is `post.ext.location` (`{ id, name, lat, lng }`, null when it has none), the usernames tagged are `post.ext.usertags`, the comments Instagram shows under the post are `post.ext.top_comments` (`{ id, text, username, likes, published_at }`) when the primary source answers, a carousel lists its slides in `post.ext.media` (`{ type, url, width, height }`), and the `#tags` and `@handles` in the caption are `post.ext.hashtags` and `post.ext.mentions`. The view count is served resiliently: Instagram removed per-post play counts from its public web pages in August 2026, so when the primary source omits the count on a video the API automatically fills engagement.views (and ext.ig_play_count) from a second source within the same request. One call, one credit, no extra endpoint needed. Co-author data is the one thing this endpoint cannot give you: the public web page behind it reports an empty co-author list on every post, including genuine collaborative ones, so `post.ext.coauthors` is deliberately omitted here rather than returned as a misleading empty array. For the co-author list of a single post use /v1/instagram/post/stats, and for a whole feed use /v1/instagram/profile/posts or /v1/instagram/profile/reels.

**Use when** you want it for the standard single post lookup, views included on video; use post/stats only when you also need the share count.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the Instagram post. A share link copied from the app (`instagram.com/share/...`) works too; a share link to a profile is refused at no charge with the handle to send, and a dead one is a free 404. · e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/p/DcCH2ZygIiP/`
- `region` (optional, string) - 2 letter country code to set the proxy in
- `trim` (optional, boolean) - Set to true to get a trimmed response
- `download_media` (optional, boolean) - Set to true to also download the video/images and get back durable hosted media URLs under `data.post.ext.download_media_urls` (`[{ post_id, cdn_url, type, cached }]`). Use these for archiving; the raw `media_urls` are short-lived signed CDN links that expire. Adds a few seconds of latency while the media is fetched. Not available on login-gated posts (age-restricted 18+ and similar), which are served by a source that cannot host durable copies: the post and its media still come back in full, and the response carries a `data._warnings` note telling you to read `data.post.content.media_urls` directly.

**Response** `Post` object at `data`, `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/Post.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.content.text` | 100% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to author profile picture |
| `post.author.display_name` | 100% | Author display name |

+19 more (types in the full schema): `post.author` {verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, views, saves, shares}; `post` {url}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.ext` {ig_play_count, repost_count}; `post.flags` {deleted, pinned}. Never filled: `post.ext.video_view_count`.

**Next** `instagram/post/comments` (`url` ← `data.post.url`) - The comments on the post. · `instagram/profile` (`handle` ← `data.post.author.username`) - The author's profile: followers, bio and counts. · `instagram/profile/posts` (`handle` ← `data.post.author.username`) - List Instagram user posts. · `instagram/profile/about` (`handle` ← `data.post.author.username`) - Get Instagram account transparency details.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/post" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DcCH2ZygIiP/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/post/comment/replies - 1-5 credits (request-shaped)

Returns replies under one Instagram comment. Each reply includes text, like count, nested reply count, author, and timestamp. Pass the post URL and the parent comment_id. Page with cursor.

**Use when** Use it after post/comments: pass the post URL and the parent comment_id to expand one thread.
**Cost** price moves with `label` · cache 300 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit per page, with the default labels (sentiment, question, purchase_intent, complaint) included free. label=spam, toxic or low_quality holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 comments that were newly judged: comments already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** cursor · ≈15/page (observed) · depth unknown · price per N items not proven · typical 2.6-5.1 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - URL of the Instagram post that holds the parent comment. A share link copied from the app (`instagram.com/share/...`) works too; a share link to a profile is refused at no charge with the handle to send, and a dead one is a free 404. · e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/reel/C8rKmYvsrck`
- `comment_id` (required) - Id of the parent comment whose replies to list. · e.g. `18038110327814211`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Cursor from the previous response to fetch the next page.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sentiment | spam | question | purchase_intent | complaint | toxic | low_quality | injection; paid: spam, toxic, low_quality, injection) · `exclude` (spam | low_quality) · `label_evidence` (1) → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality)

**Constraints**

- `exclude`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 8 comma-separated values.
- `exclude`: at most 2 comma-separated values.

**Response** `CommentList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ comment, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/CommentList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `comment.text` | Comment body. |
| `comment.id` | Platform-specific comment ID (always a string) |
| `comment.published_at` | Comment creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `comment.url` | Direct URL to the comment on the source platform |
| `comment.author.username` | Comment author username (null when tombstoned) |
| `comment.parent_id` | Parent comment ID for nested replies, or null for… |

+16 more (types in the full schema): `comment` {post_id}; `computed` {labels_evidence, language}; `comment.author` {avatar_url, verified}; `comment.engagement` {likes, replies}; `comment.flags` {deleted}; `computed.labels` {complaint, injection, low_quality, purchase_intent, question, sentiment, spam, toxic}. Never filled: `comment.author.display_name`, `comment.flags.pinned`. Page-level: `data.comment_language`, `data.comment_recency`, `data.dropped`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.label_share`, `data.labels`.

## GET /v1/instagram/post/comments - 5-19 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a list of comments on an Instagram post, ranked by the platform's own popularity order by default (`sort=top`) so the most-liked comments come first, or newest-first with `sort=recent`. Each comment includes the author, comment text, real like count, reply count, and creation timestamp. Page through with `cursor`. Note: comment.author.display_name is usually null, because the Instagram surface that serves this endpoint withholds commenter display names. Join on comment.author.username. `comment.flags.liked_by_creator` is true when the post's creator liked (hearted) the comment and false when not, and null when the source that served the call could not tell.

**Use when** you want to read the comment section of one post, paging deeper with the cursor it returns; pass sort=recent for newest first.
**Cost** price moves with `label`, `scan_pages` · cache 300 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits per page, with the default labels (sentiment, question, purchase_intent, complaint) included free. label=spam, toxic or low_quality holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 comments that were newly judged: comments already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** cursor · ≈15/page (observed) · depth unknown · price per N items not proven · typical 1.8-4.5 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - URL of the Instagram post (a /p/, /reel/, /reels/, or /tv/ link). A share link copied from the app (`instagram.com/share/...`) works too; a share link to a profile is refused at no charge with the handle to send, and a dead one is a free 404. · e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/p/DXidPIVDU6M/`
- `sort` (optional, enum: top | recent) - Ordering: `top` (default) ranks by Instagram's popularity order (most-liked first); `recent` returns newest-first. Use `recent` when you are paging through a whole thread: Instagram ranks only the most-liked head, so a `top` walk starts repeating comments once you page past it.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response to fetch the next page.
- `safe_url` (optional, boolean) - When true, returns URL-safe profile picture links suitable for embedding.
- `scan_pages` (optional, integer, 1-3) - Optional, 1 to 3, default 1. With 2 or 3, the call reads that many pages, drops comments repeated across pages, and returns them all sorted by likes (sort=top) or newest first (sort=recent). Use it when the first page of a top-sorted thread is low-like comments. Costs 5 credits for each page that added comments; a page of repeats is not billed. data.scan reports the pages read and billed and whether the thread ended.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off the page, and the page that reaches one ends the walk: `next_cursor` is not returned and `pagination.stopped_at` is `since`. Sending it sets the newest-first sort shown in this endpoint's sort parameter (any other sort value is a free 400). The page still costs what a page costs, so you pay for the pages you walk and no more. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sentiment | spam | question | purchase_intent | complaint | toxic | low_quality | injection; paid: spam, toxic, low_quality, injection) · `exclude` (spam | low_quality) · `label_evidence` (1) → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality)

**Constraints**

- `since` requires `sort=recent` (auto-injected when `sort` is absent; a different value is a free 400).
- `exclude`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 8 comma-separated values.
- `exclude`: at most 2 comma-separated values.

**Response** `CommentList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ comment, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/CommentList.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `comment.id` | 100% | Platform-specific comment ID (always a string) |
| `comment.author.username` | 100% | Comment author username (null when tombstoned) |
| `comment.text` | 93% | Comment body. |
| `comment.published_at` | 100% | Comment creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `comment.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to comment author profile picture |
| `comment.author.verified` | 100% | Whether the comment author is verified |

+16 more (types in the full schema): `comment.engagement` {likes, replies}; `comment` {url, post_id}; `computed` {labels_evidence, language}; `comment.flags` {deleted}; `computed.labels` {complaint, injection, low_quality, purchase_intent, question, sentiment, spam, toxic}; `comment.author` {display_name}. ## GET /v1/instagram/post/likers - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns a sample of the accounts that liked an Instagram post. Each liker includes username, display name, avatar URL, verification status, and profile URL, alongside the post's total like count in `total`. Instagram exposes a ranked slice rather than the whole list, usually around a thousand accounts on a popular post: the endpoint does not paginate, and `total` reflects the full like count rather than the number of retrievable likers, so expect `items.length` to be far smaller than `total` on a post with many likes. `total` can be null when the last backup source served the call, because that source reports no reliable like count; read the count from /v1/instagram/post/stats instead.

**Use when** you want to see who liked a post, accepting that Instagram exposes only about the first 100 likers however many likes the post has.

- `safe_url` (optional, boolean) - When true, returns URL-safe profile picture links suitable for embedding.

## GET /v1/instagram/post/stats - 5-9 credits (request-shaped)

Returns full engagement stats for a single Instagram post or reel: likes, comments, the view (play) count, and the share count (`engagement.shares`), which is the number shown next to the paper-plane Share icon in the app. The share count is a strong authenticity signal: unlike likes and comments, shares are hard to inflate, so it helps separate genuine reach from bought engagement. The standard /v1/instagram/post endpoint cannot return the share count. Metric availability depends on the media type: likes and comments populate on every post, but Instagram exposes a view (play) count and a share count only on video media (reels, videos, and carousels containing a video). On photo posts and photo-only carousels, `engagement.views` and `engagement.shares` are `null`, and because `computed.estimated_reach` and `computed.engagement_rate` derive from views, they are `null` there too. When Instagram's response for a reel includes the save count and the two-arrows Repost ("regram") counter, the plain call returns them at `engagement.saves` and `post.ext.repost_count`; Instagram includes them on some responses and not others, so do not rely on the plain call for them. Instagram publishes no save count and no share count on photos and carousels, so `engagement.saves` is null there on every call. Every post carries `post.ext.media_type` (`image`, `video` or `carousel`), a carousel carries its slide count at `post.ext.carousel_count`, and a reel carries Instagram's remix counter at `post.ext.remix_count` (how many reels were made from it). `include=saves` is the reliable way to get them: it asks a third source for a reel's save and repost count whenever the plain call came back without them, for 4 extra credits kept only when a save count comes back; a photo or carousel is never looked up. Use this endpoint for a single post; to get the share count for every reel or post across a whole feed in one call, use /v1/instagram/profile/reels/full or /v1/instagram/profile/posts/full. This endpoint also returns the post's collaborative-post co-authors under `post.ext.coauthors` (`{ id, username, full_name, is_verified, profile_pic_url }` per account, empty array when the post is not a collab): the standard /v1/instagram/post endpoint cannot, because its web source reports every post as having no co-authors. Pass the post `url` (a /p/, /reel/, or /tv/ link; story URLs are not accepted, list a user's active stories with /v1/instagram/stories instead).

**Use when** you need the share count for a single post, or the co-author list of one collab post; views also come on post itself, and photo posts return both numbers as null.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits for the post. include=saves holds 4 more and keeps them only when it fills a save count the plain call lacked, refunding them otherwise, so a hydrated call is at most 9 credits; on a reel whose save count the plain call already carries, and on any photo or carousel, it settles at 5. Post lookups are cached for 10 minutes.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - URL of the Instagram post (a /p/, /reel/, or /tv/ link). A share link copied from the app (`instagram.com/share/...`) works too; a share link to a profile is refused at no charge with the handle to send, and a dead one is a free 404. · e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/p/CnpPou9hWqq/`
- `safe_url` (optional, boolean) - When true, returns URL-safe media links suitable for embedding.
- `include` (optional, enum: saves) - Set to `saves` (one token only) to ask a third source for a reel's save count (`post.engagement.saves`) and repost count (`post.ext.repost_count`) when the plain call returned without them. 4 extra credits, kept only when a save count comes back; a repeat within the cache window is 0. Photos and carousels are never looked up, because Instagram publishes no save count on them. Adds 3 to 6 seconds when a lookup runs; read `data.hydration` for the credits held and kept and the time.

**Response** `Post` object at `data`, `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/Post.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+19 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, saves, shares, views}; `post.ext` {author_id, ig_play_count, repost_count}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Page-level: `data.hydration`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/post/stats" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CnpPou9hWqq/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/profile - 1 credit (standard)

Returns public profile information for an Instagram user including the exact integer follower count, following count, bio, profile picture URL, and verification status. `author.posts_count` is the account's lifetime post count, for accounts of any size, in the same call and for the same 1 credit. In the rare case that count cannot be read in time the leaf is null rather than a wrong number, and a repeat call normally fills it. Age-restricted (18+) profiles are supported. Every link in the bio is listed in `author.ext.bio_links` (`{ title, url, link_type }`, the direct address), the Facebook-side id of the account is `author.ext.fbid`, and `author.ext.is_business` says whether it is an Instagram business account. `author.ext.hd_avatar_url` is the full-size profile picture. When the account publishes a contact address in its bio, it is returned as `author.ext.public_email`; otherwise that leaf is null. Instagram's in-app tap-to-email button is not readable from any public surface, so the bio is the only source for it. To vet a creator by market, call /v1/instagram/profile/about instead: it returns the follower count and the declared country in one call, at the same price, so there is no need to call both.

**Use when** you want it for a quick snapshot by handle; profile/full adds recent posts and computed metrics, and profile/about adds country, month joined and contact.
**Cost** cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - Instagram username without the @ symbol · e.g. `instagram`
- `trim` (optional, boolean) - Set to true to get a trimmed response
- `contact_email` (optional, enum: 1) - Optional. When 1, also returns author.ext.contact_email: when the bio lists two or more email addresses, the one the creator gives for contacting them personally, copied verbatim from the bio. Null when there is one address or none, when every address belongs to a manager, agency or brand, or when the choice was not confident. author.ext.public_email is unchanged. No extra credits.

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `author.id` | 100% | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.username` | 100% | User handle or username |
| `author.url` | 100% | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | 100% | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | 100% | Display name or full name |

+13 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, verified, private, posts_count}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `author.ext` {contact_email, hd_avatar_url, business_category}. Also in the sample: `author` {last_post_at string}. Never filled: `author.joined_at`, `author.likes_count`.

**Next** `instagram/profile/posts` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - The account's latest posts. · `instagram/highlights` (`user_id` ← `data.author.id`) - The account's story highlights. · `instagram/stories` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - The account's current stories. · `instagram/profile/posts/full` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - Instagram posts with views, likes, comments, and per-post share counts where available, in one call.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=instagram" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/profile/about - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the data behind Instagram's "About this account" panel for a public account: the country the account is based in (`author.ext.country`), the month it joined (`author.ext.account_created`), and the public contact address and phone the account publishes (`author.ext.public_email`, `author.ext.public_phone`). Country is the account's own declared country, not the country you are calling from. The same call returns the profile itself: follower and following counts (`author.followers`), bio, avatar, verification, and the account's lifetime post count as `author.posts_count`. It gives the follower count and the declared country in one call, so there is no need to call /v1/instagram/profile as well. Coverage follows what Instagram publishes: an account that shows no transparency panel returns null for those fields. `author.ext.former_usernames_count` is how many former usernames the panel lists, 0 when it lists none, so a count above 0 tells you the handle was renamed at least once (the old names themselves are not published). Send `include=verified_at` to add `author.ext.verified_at`, the month Instagram verified the account as the panel shows it ("April 2024"), null when the account is not verified or the panel shows no date. Only one source serves `include=verified_at`, so when it is unavailable the call returns an error at no charge rather than a profile without the date; the same request without it still works.

**Use when** you need an account's total post count, or to tell where a creator is based, for example to include or exclude a region.
**Cost** cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit per call, with or without `include=verified_at`. A call that fails, a handle that does not exist and a refused parameter cost nothing.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - Instagram username without the @ symbol · e.g. `instagram`
- `include` (optional, string) - Send `verified_at` to add `author.ext.verified_at`, the month Instagram verified the account ("April 2024"). Same price. Any other value is a free 400.

**Constraints**

- `include`: at most 1 comma-separated values; each value one of verified_at.

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |
| `author.followers` | Follower or subscriber count as an integer. |

+15 more (types in the full schema): `author` {following, posts_count, verified, private}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `author.ext` {account_created, business_category, country, hd_avatar_url, public_email, public_phone}. Also in the sample: `author` {url string}. Never filled: `author.joined_at`, `author.likes_count`.

**Next** `instagram/profile/posts` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - List Instagram user posts. · `instagram/profile/reels` (`user_id` ← `data.author.id`) - List Instagram user reels. · `instagram/profile/posts/full` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - Instagram posts with views, likes, comments, and per-post share counts where available, in one call. · `instagram/profile/full` (`handle` ← `data.author.username`) - Instagram profile, recent posts, and computed analytics in one call.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/about" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=instagram" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/profile/country - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the country an Instagram account declares on its "About this account" panel (`author.ext.country`), the month it joined (`author.ext.account_created`), its username, its profile link and its verified flag, for 1 credit. Pass the numeric account id as `user_id`: every Instagram search row carries it as `post.ext.author_id`, and /v1/instagram/profile/about returns it as `author.id`. Country is the account's own declared country, not where a post was filmed and not the country you are calling from, and it is null when the account shows no transparency panel. This endpoint reads the panel only, so followers, bio, avatar, posts count and the public email and phone are not on it; for those, call /v1/instagram/profile/about with the username. A username is refused at no charge with a pointer to /v1/instagram/profile/about. Only one source serves this read, so there is no second source to fall back to when it is unavailable.

**Use when** you want to check where the creators on a search page are based, 1 credit each, by passing post.ext.author_id; for a username, use profile/about.
**Cost** cache 2592000 s
**Pricing** 1 credit per call. A refused username or a missing `user_id` costs nothing.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `user_id` (optional, string) - The numeric Instagram account id, for example `post.ext.author_id` from a search row or `author.id` from /v1/instagram/profile/about. A username is refused at no charge. · e.g. `25025320`

**Constraints**

- `user_id` is required (it is optional in shape only - the request needs it).

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.verified` | Whether the account is verified |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |
| `computed.estimated_reach` | Estimated reach based on views or follower count. |

+4 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {language, save_rate}; `author.ext` {account_created, country}. Never filled: `author.avatar_url`, `author.bio`, `author.display_name`, `author.external_url`, `author.followers`, `author.following`, `author.joined_at`, `author.last_post_at`, `author.likes_count`, `author.location`, `author.posts_count`, `author.private`.
