## GET /v1/instagram/profile/full - 5 credits (custom)

Fans out to the Instagram profile and recent-posts endpoints in parallel and returns the unified author, the recent-post list, and computed metrics: avg_engagement_rate, avg_engagement_rate_by_followers, posting cadence (with the window it was measured over), the top post, and the format mix. avg_engagement_rate is view-based: the mean of each post's (likes + comments + shares) / views, so only posts that carry a view count contribute, and it is null when none does. avg_engagement_rate_by_followers is the mean of likes + comments per post divided by the account's follower count, over every post that carries both, so it covers posts with no view count. One call reads one page of recent posts, which on Instagram is 12 posts, and computes the metrics over that page: `posts` can shorten the window but not lengthen it past one page, and `_warnings` says so when fewer posts came back than `posts` asked for. Pass `posts_cursor` back as `cursor` to read the next page, 5 credits a call. The profile leg is the only critical leg: if posts can't be fetched the call still returns the profile with post-dependent metrics null, and every leg's status is surfaced in legs[]. Flat 5 credits. Photo and carousel rows have no view count, because Instagram does not publish one on stills, and neither does a video whose owner hides like and view counts. On a mostly-photo grid avg_engagement_rate is therefore null and `_warnings` says why: read avg_engagement_rate_by_followers, which uses the same formula as `computed.engagement_rate` on `/v1/instagram/profile`. Share counts are on `/v1/instagram/profile/posts/full` and `/v1/instagram/post/stats`, not this call.

**Use when** Use it instead of calling profile and profile/posts separately; the profile still comes back if posts cannot be fetched, with post metrics null.
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 8.5-16 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username or handle, with or without a leading @. One of the identity params is required. · e.g. `mrbeast`
- `posts` (optional, integer) - How many of the fetched recent posts to return and compute the metrics over (1-100, default 25). One call reads one page, which on Instagram is 12 posts, so a larger value returns that page and a `_warnings` note; pass posts_cursor back as cursor for the next page. · e.g. `25`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pass a prior response's posts_cursor to read the next page of posts. Each call is a separate 5-credit call whose metrics cover that page only.
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV subset of posts,computed (default both). include=computed omits the raw posts[] array from the response to save payload. The metrics are computed from the same fetched posts either way, so they do not change.

**Constraints**

- `handle` is required (it is optional in shape only - the request needs it).

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `profile` {id string, username string, display_name string, avatar_url string, bio string, verified boolean, followers number, following number, posts_count number, likes_count null, url string, private boolean, joined_at null, last_post_at string}; `profile.ext` {business_category null}; `posts[].post` {id string, url string}; `posts[].post.content` {text string, media_urls string[], thumbnail_url null, duration_seconds null}; `posts[].post.author` {username string, display_name string, avatar_url string, verified boolean} (+35 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/full" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=mrbeast" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/profile/posts - 1-29 credits (request-shaped)

Returns the public posts on an Instagram profile, newest first. Paging the cursor continues through that grid until it ends. Each post includes the written caption, the post URL, the media type, the post date, the like count and the comment count. Instagram is currently returning two record widths on this surface, and the narrow one carries no like count, no comment count, no post date and no author display name. When a whole page comes back narrow, the page is served from a second source that carries all four, at the same price, and its `next_cursor` continues on that source. If no second source answers, the narrow page is returned rather than an error, so those leaves can still be null on a page. Every row still carries its id, URL and caption. Every row also carries `post.ext.media_type` (`image`, `video` or `carousel`), a carousel carries its slide count at `post.ext.carousel_count`, and `post.flags.pinned` says whether the owner pinned the post to the top of the grid. The pins are read when you send `exclude_pinned=true`, at the same price: the pinned posts are left out and the rows kept carry `post.flags.pinned: false`. A row the pin read did not reach, or a page where only a source that cannot mark pins answered, carries `post.flags.pinned: null`, is kept, and `data._warnings` says so. Without `exclude_pinned`, `post.flags.pinned` is null on rows from the first source, whose record carries no pin data. `recent_days=N` keeps only posts from the last N days and stops the pagination once a page reaches older posts, so walking a feed back to a date window needs no manual stop. Send `include=audio` to add the sound each video uses: `post.ext.music_id`, the id /v1/instagram/audio/reels takes, and `post.ext.music` (`{ id, track_title, artist, is_original }`), for 1 extra credit per video filled. Every row carries the place the post is tagged at as `post.ext.location` (`{ id, name, lat, lng }`, null when the post has no place), a carousel lists its slides in `post.ext.media` (`{ type, url, width, height }`), and the `#tags` and `@handles` in the caption are listed in `post.ext.hashtags` and `post.ext.mentions`. Send `include=tags` to add `post.ext.usertags`, the usernames tagged in each post, for 1 extra credit per post that names someone. When you need the engagement for a specific post, pass its URL to /v1/instagram/post/stats; for a whole feed with share counts merged in, use /v1/instagram/profile/posts/full. Collaborative posts (Instagram's native "Collab" feature) are fully resolved: `post.ext.coauthors` lists every co-author account as `{ id, username, full_name, is_verified, profile_pic_url }`. Read it whenever you list a profile: a collab post has a single producer and appears in every co-author's grid, so `post.author` is whichever account created the post and is not always the handle you queried. The complete set of accounts on a post is `post.author.username` plus every `username` in `post.ext.coauthors`. An empty array means Instagram reports the post as not a collab; on a narrow record the key is absent rather than empty, which means the question was not answered for that row, so treat absent and `[]` as different. Note: engagement.shares is null on this endpoint (the upstream carries no per-post share count); to additionally merge in per-post share counts where a second source exposes them (coverage varies by account), use /v1/instagram/profile/posts/full. With trim=true the upstream record is the narrow one, so the page is normally served from the second source described at the top and carries every field above. A trimmed page served as it is omits `post.ext.coauthors` and leaves `post.flags.pinned` null, because the trimmed record carries neither signal.

**Use when** you want it for a plain feed pull; profile/posts/full adds per-post share counts. On a collab post the author is whoever created it, so read ext.coauthors for everyone on it.
**Cost** price moves with `include`, `label` · cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit per page. include=audio holds 1 more per row, up to 12, and keeps it only for each video whose sound came back, refunding the rest, so a page costs at most 13 credits and a page with no videos costs 1. include=tags holds 1 more per row, up to 12, and keeps it only for each post whose tagged accounts came back, refunding the rest; with both tokens a page costs at most 25 credits. exclude_pinned and recent_days do not change the price of a page. The default labels (sponsored, intent, niche) are free. label=mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection, or label=intent with offer=, holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 posts that were newly judged: posts already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** cursor (native `next_max_id`) · ≈12/page (observed once) · depth unknown · price per N items not proven · typical 7.3-13 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - Instagram username without the @ symbol · e.g. `instagram`
- `since` (optional, string) - Only posts published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Older posts are left off the page, and the page that reaches one ends the walk: `next_cursor` is not returned and `pagination.stopped_at` is `since`. Pinned posts sit out of date order and never end the walk. The page still costs what a page costs, so a daily poll pays for the pages it walks and no more. · e.g. `2026-09-01`
- `stop_at_id` (optional, string) - The id (`post.id`) or URL (`post.url`) of the newest post you already hold. The page stops just before it: that post and everything after it are left off, `next_cursor` is not returned, and `pagination.stopped_at` is `known_id`. A pinned post never counts as the stop point. If it is not on this page the page is returned in full with its cursor, so keep walking. `pagination.stopped_at` is `end` when the list ran out first and `null` while there is more to walk. A post counts as pinned when `post.flags.pinned` is true or when it is older than a post below it on the page, so a pinned post that also sits in date order is never the stop point on a page that marks pins, and can be on a page whose `post.flags.pinned` is null.
- `next_max_id` (optional, string) - Cursor to get next page of results.
- `trim` (optional, boolean) - Set to true to request the lighter upstream record. That record is the narrow width described above, so the page is normally served from the second source with every field. A trimmed page served as it is omits `post.ext.coauthors`, and its `post.flags.pinned` is null, as it is on any page called without `exclude_pinned`. The price is the same either way.
- `exclude_pinned` (optional, boolean) - Set to true to leave out the posts the owner pinned to the top of the profile. The pins are read from a second source alongside the page, at the same price, and the rows kept carry `post.flags.pinned: false`. A row whose pin state is unknown (`post.flags.pinned: null`), such as a row that pin read did not reach, a trimmed row, or a page from a source that cannot mark pins, is kept, and `data._warnings` says so. Without this parameter `post.flags.pinned` is not read and is null on rows from the first source.
- `recent_days` (optional, integer, 1-3650) - Keep only posts published in the last N days (1 to 3650). Older posts are removed from the page, pinned ones included, and once a page reaches posts older than the window `next_cursor` is not returned, so a walk back to a date window stops on its own. The page still costs what a page costs.
- `include` (optional, string) - `audio` adds `post.ext.music_id` and `post.ext.music` to video rows from a second lookup: 1 extra credit per video filled, refunded when the sound could not be read. Photos and carousels are never looked up. `tags` adds `post.ext.usertags`, the usernames tagged in the post, to every row from a second lookup: 1 extra credit per post that names someone, refunded for a post that tags nobody or whose lookup failed. Both tokens can be combined (`include=audio,tags`). Adds a few seconds; read `data.hydration` for the credits held and kept and the time.
- `ai_written_threshold` (optional, string) - Optional, only with label=ai_written and exclude=ai_written. The p (0 to 1) at which exclude=ai_written drops a post. Default 0.95 (level likely). 0.71 also drops possible posts: more AI posts go, and more posts by people with them.
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sponsored | mention | intent | niche | quality | ai_style | ai_written | injection; paid: mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection) · `exclude` (engagement_bait | ai_style | ai_written) · `label_evidence` (1) · `brand` · `brand_description` · `offer` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality)

**Constraints**

- `ai_written_threshold` is a no-op without `label` - sending it alone is a free 400.
- `exclude`, `brand`, `brand_description`, `offer`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `include`: at most 2 comma-separated values; each value one of audio | tags.
- `label`: at most 8 comma-separated values.
- `exclude`: at most 3 comma-separated values.

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.url` | 100% | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | 100% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to author profile picture |

+28 more (types in the full schema): `post.author` {display_name, verified}; `post.content` {media_urls, duration_seconds}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, views}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, labels_evidence, language}; `computed.labels` {ai_style, ai_written, injection, intent, mention, niche, quality} (+9 more). Never filled: `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.creator_baseline`, `data.dropped`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.hydration`, `data.labels`.

**Next** `instagram/post/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - The comments on each post. · `instagram/post` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Full details and stats for each post. · `instagram/post/stats` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Current like, comment and view counts for each post. · `instagram/media/screen-text` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post on-screen text.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/posts" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=instagram" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/profile/posts/full - 5-25 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a creator's recent posts with views, likes, comments, and the per-post share count merged in wherever the upstream exposes it: in a single call. The standard /v1/instagram/profile/posts endpoint returns views/likes/comments but leaves engagement.shares null (its upstream has no per-post reshare count); this composite fans out to a second mobile source that carries the share number and merges it back onto each item by post id. Share coverage is best-effort and varies by account: the mobile source only exposes reshare_count for the items it returns, so some (sometimes most) items keep engagement.shares null. That null means "upstream doesn't expose it", not "zero". Read shares_coverage (the fraction of returned items that got a real share number) before relying on shares; legs[] shows each leg's status. Billing: the standard leg is critical (its failure refunds the full call); the shares leg is best-effort: if it fails OUTRIGHT the items still return with shares null and 4 of the 5 credits are refunded (you pay the standard 1-credit list price). A successful shares leg with low coverage is still the flat 5 credits, since the second source was queried regardless of how many items it happened to cover. Paginate with next_cursor.

**Use when** share counts matter across a whole feed; profile/posts is the lighter choice when likes and comments are enough.
**Cost** price moves with `limit` · cache 600 s
**Pricing** 5 credits per upstream page of about 12 posts. With no `limit` that is one page and a flat 5 credits. With `limit` set the composite walks `ceil(limit / 12)` pages - 3 for limit=30, 5 for the 50 maximum, so 25 credits at the top - holds that many up front and refunds every page it did not need. One partial refund sits inside the per-page price: a shares leg that fails outright refunds 4 of the 5 credits for that page, leaving the 1-credit list price. A shares leg that succeeds with low coverage is still the full 5, because the second source was queried either way. A `user_id` call is priced exactly like a `handle` call.
**Paging** cursor · 12/page; `limit` is a collect-until-N row target (max 50), not a page size - `limit` (1-50) walks upstream pages server-side until that many items are collected, billing per page of ~12 consumed (5 credits each, 5-25 total). It is not a page size. · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/12) x 5 credits · typical 7.4-16 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username (with or without a leading @). Required unless user_id is given. · e.g. `sid.and.listen`
- `user_id` (optional, string) - Numeric Instagram user id. Alternative to handle: the account's username is looked up from the id first, so a user_id call returns the same items, share counts and price as a handle call. An id that matches no account returns 404 and is not charged.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor to page deeper.
- `limit` (optional, integer) - Return up to this many items in one call (1-50). The endpoint pages the underlying source server-side until it has collected this many (or runs out), and bills per upstream page consumed (5 credits/page). Omit for a single page.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `handle`, `user_id`.

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (inferred from a sample): `post` {id string, url string, published_at string}; `post.content` {text string, media_urls string, thumbnail_url string, duration_seconds number}; `post.author` {username string, display_name string, avatar_url string, verified boolean}; `post.engagement` {views number, likes number, comments number, shares number, saves null}; `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned boolean, deleted boolean}; `post.ext` {author_id string, media_type string, published_at_epoch number, coauthors array, shares_source string} (+4 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/posts/full" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=sid.and.listen" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/profile/reels - 1-18 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a list of reels posted by an Instagram user. Each reel includes view count, like count, comment count, and thumbnail. Every row carries `post.ext.media_type` (`video`) and the remix counter Instagram shows at `post.ext.remix_count`, the number of reels made from this one. A reel that uses licensed music carries `post.ext.music_id`, the id /v1/instagram/audio/reels takes, and `post.ext.music` (`{ id, track_title, artist, is_original }`) on the plain call; send `include=audio` to add the same two leaves on reels that use an original sound, for 1 extra credit per reel filled. Send `include=stats` for the full stat line on every reel of the page, for 1 extra credit a page: `engagement.shares`, `engagement.saves` and `post.ext.repost_count` beside views, likes, comments and the remix counter, `post.ext.music_id` for every reel whatever its sound, and `post.ext.audio_cluster_id`, Instagram's audio cluster for the reel (the id Instagram uses to group different uploads of the same sound; the plain call does not carry it). `exclude_pinned=true` leaves out the reels pinned to the top of the reels tab, and `recent_days=N` keeps only reels from the last N days and stops the pagination once a page reaches older reels. Collaborative reels (Instagram's native "Collab" feature) carry the full co-author list under `post.ext.coauthors` as `{ id, username, full_name, is_verified, profile_pic_url }`; `post.author` stays the producing account, which on a collab is not always the handle you queried. An empty array means Instagram reports the reel as not a collab; on a narrow record the key is absent rather than empty, which means the question was not answered for that row, so treat absent and `[]` as different. Note: engagement.shares is null on this endpoint (the upstream carries no per-post share count); to additionally merge in per-reel share counts where a second source exposes them (coverage varies by account), use /v1/instagram/profile/reels/full. With trim=true you get a lighter record: the engagement, the author, the caption, the timestamp and the reel URL are all still returned, but `post.content.media_urls` is null because the trimmed record carries no video file, `post.content.duration_seconds` is null, `post.ext.coauthors` is omitted and `post.flags.pinned` is null. The cover image is returned as `post.content.thumbnail_url` either way. Leave trim unset when you need the video URL or the duration. Instagram is currently serving two record shapes on this endpoint and one of them omits the caption, so `post.content.text` can be null on a page where the reel plainly has one; re-request to get a page from the fuller shape, or read the caption from /v1/instagram/post. Send `sort=most_viewed` for Instagram's own most viewed reels tab: the creator's reels in the order Instagram ranks them by plays, highest first, which reaches back years and can surface reels the default page leaves out. It is Instagram's ranking, served as it comes, so an occasional reel can sit out of strict order. Every row has the same fields as the default page. Only one source serves this order, so when it is unavailable the call returns an error at no charge rather than reels in another order, and its `next_cursor` only continues a `sort=most_viewed` walk. It cannot be combined with `include`, `trim`, `recent_days`, `since` or `stop_at_id`, which read the default newest-first page; that is a free 400. On a reel also posted to Facebook, `engagement.views` can include its Facebook views: `post.ext.instagram_views` is the Instagram-only figure, the same on every Instagram endpoint, and `post.ext.facebook_views` is the Facebook part when the source reports it.

**Use when** you want it for reels only rather than the whole post feed; use profile/reels/full when you also need per-reel share counts.
**Cost** price moves with `include`, `label` · cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit per page. include=stats adds 1 credit a page. include=audio holds 1 more per row, up to 12, and keeps it only for each video whose sound came back, refunding the rest; with include=stats every reel already carries its sound, so the audio join costs nothing more. A page costs at most 14 credits. exclude_pinned and recent_days do not change the price of a page. sort=most_viewed costs the same 1 credit a page. The default labels (sponsored, intent, niche) are free. label=mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection, or label=intent with offer=, holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 posts that were newly judged: posts already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** cursor (native `max_id`) · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 4.7-12 s

**Query params**

- `since` (optional, string) - Only reels published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Older reels are left off the page, and the page that reaches one ends the walk: `next_cursor` is not returned and `pagination.stopped_at` is `since`. Pinned reels sit out of date order and never end the walk. The page still costs what a page costs, so a daily poll pays for the pages it walks and no more. · e.g. `2026-09-01`
- `user_id` (optional, string) - Instagram user id. Use this for faster response times.
- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username without the @ symbol · e.g. `mrbeast`
- `max_id` (optional, string) - Max id to get more reels. Get 'max_id' from previous response.
- `trim` (optional, boolean) - Set to true to request the lighter upstream record: a smaller, faster page that keeps the engagement, the author, the caption, the timestamp and the reel URL. What it drops is `post.content.media_urls` (the video file), `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.ext.coauthors` and `post.flags.pinned`. The cover image is returned as `post.content.thumbnail_url` either way. Leave it unset when you need the video URL or the duration.
- `exclude_pinned` (optional, boolean) - Set to true to leave out the posts the owner pinned to the top of the profile. A row whose pin state is unknown, which is every row with trim=true, is kept.
- `recent_days` (optional, integer, 1-3650) - Keep only posts published in the last N days (1 to 3650). Older posts are removed from the page, pinned ones included, and once a page reaches posts older than the window `next_cursor` is not returned, so a walk back to a date window stops on its own. The page still costs what a page costs.
- `include` (optional, string) - `stats` returns the full stat line on every reel for 1 extra credit a page: `engagement.shares`, `engagement.saves` and `post.ext.repost_count` beside views, likes, comments, the remix counter, `post.ext.music_id` for original sounds and licensed music alike, and `post.ext.audio_cluster_id`, Instagram's audio cluster for the reel. It is served by a second source, so a cursor from a request without it cannot continue a walk with it; start from page 1. `audio` adds `post.ext.music_id` and `post.ext.music` to reels still missing them from a second lookup: 1 extra credit per reel filled, refunded when the sound could not be read. Both tokens can be combined (`include=audio,stats`).
- `sort` (optional, enum: most_viewed) - Send `most_viewed` for the creator's reels in Instagram's most viewed order (highest plays first) instead of newest first. Same price. Its cursors only continue a `sort=most_viewed` walk. Cannot be combined with `include`, `trim`, `recent_days`, `since` or `stop_at_id`.
- `ai_written_threshold` (optional, string) - Optional, only with label=ai_written and exclude=ai_written. The p (0 to 1) at which exclude=ai_written drops a post. Default 0.95 (level likely). 0.71 also drops possible posts: more AI posts go, and more posts by people with them.
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sponsored | mention | intent | niche | quality | ai_style | ai_written | injection; paid: mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection) · `exclude` (engagement_bait | ai_style | ai_written) · `label_evidence` (1) · `brand` · `brand_description` · `offer` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality); `stop_at_id` → [incremental sync](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `user_id`, `handle`.
- `ai_written_threshold` is a no-op without `label` - sending it alone is a free 400.
- `exclude`, `brand`, `brand_description`, `offer`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `include`: at most 2 comma-separated values; each value one of audio | stats.
- `label`: at most 8 comma-separated values.
- `exclude`: at most 3 comma-separated values.

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.url` | 100% | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | 100% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to author profile picture |

+27 more (types in the full schema): `post.author` {display_name, verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, views}; `post.ext` {music_id}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, labels_evidence, language}; `computed.labels` {ai_style, ai_written, injection, intent, mention, niche} (+8 more). Never filled: `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.creator_baseline`, `data.dropped`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.hydration`, `data.labels`.

**Next** `instagram/post/stats` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post stats including the share count. · `instagram/audio/reels` (`audio_id` ← `data.items[].post.ext.music_id`; needs `include=audio` on this call) - List Instagram reels using an audio track.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/reels" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=mrbeast" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/profile/reels/full - 5-25 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a creator's recent reels with views, likes, comments, and the per-reel share count merged in wherever the upstream exposes it: in a single call. The standard /v1/instagram/profile/reels endpoint returns views/likes/comments but leaves engagement.shares null (its upstream has no per-post reshare count); this composite fans out to a second mobile source that carries the share number and merges it back onto each item by post id. Share coverage is best-effort and varies by account: the mobile source only exposes reshare_count for the items it returns, so some (sometimes most) items keep engagement.shares null. That null means "upstream doesn't expose it", not "zero". Read shares_coverage (the fraction of returned items that got a real share number) before relying on shares; legs[] shows each leg's status. Billing: the standard leg is critical (its failure refunds the full call); the shares leg is best-effort: if it fails OUTRIGHT the items still return with shares null and 4 of the 5 credits are refunded (you pay the standard 1-credit list price). A successful shares leg with low coverage is still the flat 5 credits, since the second source was queried regardless of how many items it happened to cover. Paginate with next_cursor.

**Use when** share counts matter across a creator's reels; profile/reels is the lighter choice when views, likes, and comments are enough.
**Cost** price moves with `limit` · cache 600 s
**Pricing** 5 credits per upstream page of about 12 reels. With no `limit` that is one page and a flat 5 credits. With `limit` set the composite walks `ceil(limit / 12)` pages - 3 for limit=30, 5 for the 50 maximum, so 25 credits at the top - holds that many up front and refunds every page it did not need. One partial refund sits inside the per-page price: a shares leg that fails outright refunds 4 of the 5 credits for that page, leaving the 1-credit list price. A shares leg that succeeds with low coverage is still the full 5, because the second source was queried either way. A `user_id` call is priced exactly like a `handle` call.
**Paging** cursor · 12/page; `limit` is a collect-until-N row target (max 50), not a page size - `limit` (1-50) walks upstream pages server-side until that many items are collected, billing per page of ~12 consumed (5 credits each, 5-25 total). It is not a page size. · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/12) x 5 credits · typical 20-34 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username (with or without a leading @). Required unless user_id is given. · e.g. `sid.and.listen`
- `user_id` (optional, string) - Numeric Instagram user id. Alternative to handle: the account's username is looked up from the id first, so a user_id call returns the same items, share counts and price as a handle call. An id that matches no account returns 404 and is not charged.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor to page deeper.
- `limit` (optional, integer) - Return up to this many items in one call (1-50). The endpoint pages the underlying source server-side until it has collected this many (or runs out), and bills per upstream page consumed (5 credits/page). Omit for a single page.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `handle`, `user_id`.

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (inferred from a sample): `post` {id string, url string, published_at string}; `post.content` {text string, media_urls string, thumbnail_url string, duration_seconds number}; `post.author` {username string, display_name string, avatar_url string, verified boolean}; `post.engagement` {views number, likes number, comments number, shares number, saves null}; `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned boolean, deleted boolean}; `post.ext` {author_id string, media_type string, remix_count number, published_at_epoch number, coauthors array} (+5 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/reels/full" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=sid.and.listen" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/reels/trending - 5 credits (advanced)

Fetches trending reels from Instagram's public reels page. Instagram returns a small batch per call and results can overlap, so call repeatedly to discover more: duplicates are expected. Each item includes shortcode, URL, caption, media URLs, like and comment counts, and user info. There is no region or country option: Instagram assembles this feed for the account viewing it, not for a place, so the mix is global (measured 13/09/2026: a region hint changed the batch no more than a repeat call did). For region-scoped Instagram posts, find places with /v1/instagram/search/location and page their posts with /v1/instagram/location/posts. Note: engagement.views and content.duration_seconds are null on this endpoint. Instagram sends the play-count and duration keys on the trending surface with no value in them (measured null on 31 of 31 items), and no other source serves this feed, so a view count is not available here: pass a result URL to /v1/instagram/post for a per-reel view count, or use /v1/instagram/search/reels, which is sourced from a surface that still carries play counts.

**Use when** you want to sample global trends; it takes no region. Call again to see more. For one region, page location/posts after search/location.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+11 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `post.content` {media_urls}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Never filled: `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.content.thumbnail_url`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.engagement.views`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.pinned`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.dropped`.

**Next** `instagram/post/stats` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post stats including the share count.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/reels/trending" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns mixed Instagram search matches for a query: accounts, hashtags, and places in one payload, the same mix Instagram's own search box shows. It matches account, hashtag and place names, not the text of posts, so a multi-word topic sentence usually matches nothing and answers 404. For posts about a topic or keyword, use `GET /v1/instagram/search/reels?query=`.

**Use when** you need the same mixed results Instagram's search box shows; search/profiles, search/hashtag, and search/location split those types. **Not for** posts or reels (instagram/search/hashtag, instagram/search/reels), or for only profiles (instagram/search/profiles) or only places (instagram/search/location).
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - An account, hashtag or place name as typed in Instagram's search box (a name, not a topic sentence). For posts about a topic use instagram/search/reels. · e.g. `nike`

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {query string, keywords array, rank_token string}; `users[]` {position number, id string, username string, full_name string, is_verified boolean, profile_pic_url string}; `hashtags[]` {position number, id string, name string, media_count number, search_result_subtitle null}; `places[]` {position number, id string, name string, title string, subtitle string, facebook_places_id string}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=nike" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search/hashtag - 5-35 credits (request-shaped)

Flat 5 credits a page (plus 1 per creator with `include=country`), and it takes no `limit` or `max_items` (both are ignored); volume is set by `type` and `max_pages`. For keyword, topic or brand discovery (posts about a phrase), use `GET /v1/instagram/search/reels?query=` instead: 1 credit a page with view counts. Use this endpoint only when you already have a specific hashtag. For the hashtag's exact post count, call /v1/instagram/hashtag?hashtag=<tag> (1 credit). Returns recent public Instagram posts for a hashtag from Instagram's native hashtag feed. Each post includes shortcode, URL, caption, media URLs, engagement counts, and the author. Pass `type` to choose the ranking (`top`, `recent`, or `clips` for reels only). Only `type=recent` paginates: forward its `next_cursor` together with `type=recent` to page deeper. `top` and `clips` are one ranked page each, so they return `has_more: false` and no cursor; to cover more ground with those rankings, query more hashtags. A hashtag feed mixes photos and reels, so engagement.views is a number on the video rows and null on the photo rows. Pass `type=clips` for a reels-only page where every row carries a view count. Note: post.author.display_name is not available on this endpoint, so join on post.author.username, or pass it to /v1/instagram/profile?handle= for the name. Note: engagement.shares and engagement.saves are null on this endpoint (neither hashtag upstream carries a per-post share or save count); for a per-post share count pass a result URL to /v1/instagram/post/stats. Saves are platform-private. Instagram exposes no numeric save metric on any surface, and it is never fabricated. On a reel also posted to Facebook, `engagement.views` can include its Facebook views: `post.ext.instagram_views` is the Instagram-only figure, the same on every Instagram endpoint, and `post.ext.facebook_views` is the Facebook part when the source reports it.

**Use when** Use it only for a hashtag you already have: flat 5 credits, no limit or max_items. For keyword or topic discovery use instagram/search/reels. Pick type top, recent or clips; page with cursor. **Not for** keyword or topic discovery or a free text phrase (instagram/search/reels), accounts (instagram/search/profiles) or share counts (video posts) at instagram/post/stats.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** Flat 5 credits per page. `limit` and `max_items` are not parameters of this endpoint and are ignored, so they do not lower the price; `max_pages` (1 to 5) walks more pages at 5 credits each. For keyword or topic discovery, `instagram/search/reels?query=` is 1 credit a page. `include=country` holds 30 more credits a page and keeps 1 per creator whose declared country came back, refunding a creator who publishes none or cannot be found, so a page with it costs 5 to 35. With `max_pages`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free). With `seen`, a page's price falls with its share of rows you already received under that id; credits for joined data (`include=`) are never discounted.
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 4.1-9.2 s

**Query params**

- `hashtag` (required) - The hashtag to search for. The leading # is optional. · e.g. `makeup`
- `type` (optional, enum: top | recent | clips) - Ranking of the returned posts: `top` (default), `recent`, or `clips` (reels only). Only `recent` pages: `top` and `clips` are one ranked page each and return `has_more: false`.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor for `type=recent` only. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response and send the same `type` again. `top` and `clips` return no cursor.
- `safe_url` (optional, boolean) - When true, returns URL-safe media links suitable for embedding.
- `include` (optional, enum: country) - Send `country` to add each post's creator country as `post.ext.author_country`: the country the creator declares on Instagram's About this account panel, not where the post was filmed, and null when the creator publishes none. Every row carries the creator's numeric id as `post.ext.author_id`, which is what it is read by. 1 extra credit per creator whose country came back; two posts by one creator cost one lookup, a creator looked up in the last 30 days is free, and a creator who publishes none or cannot be found is refunded. A typo is a free 400.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-5) · `seen` · `min_views` (min 0) · `max_age_days` (1-3650) · `sort_rows` (views) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.url` | 100% | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.content.text` | 100% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to author profile picture |

+17 more (types in the full schema): `post.author` {verified}; `post.content` {media_urls, duration_seconds, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, views}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.ext` {author_country, author_followers, author_id}; `post.flags` {deleted, pinned}. Also in the sample: `post.ext` {media_type string, published_at_epoch number} (+1 more). Never filled: `post.author.display_name`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.hydration`, `data.walk`.

**Next** `instagram/profile` (`handle` ← `data.items[].post.author.username`) - The author's profile: followers, bio and counts. · `instagram/post/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - List Instagram post comments. · `instagram/post` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post details. · `instagram/media/transcript` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram media transcript.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/search/hashtag" \
  --data-urlencode "hashtag=makeup" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search/location - 5 credits (advanced)

Searches Instagram locations by keyword. Returns matching places, each with location.pk, a name, and coordinates, plus a display title and subtitle. There is no location.id. Pass location.pk as location_id to the Instagram location posts endpoint. location.facebook_places_id is another identifier for the same place.

**Use when** you want to pass location.pk as location_id on location/posts. location.facebook_places_id is the same place's other id. **Not for** the posts at a place (instagram/location/posts); this only finds the place and its id.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search keyword or phrase to find Instagram locations. · e.g. `Paris`

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ location, title, subtitle }` (inferred from a sample): `location` {pk number, facebook_places_id number, external_source string, name string, address string, city null, has_viewer_saved boolean, short_name string, lng number, lat number}; {title string, subtitle string}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/search/location" \
  --data-urlencode "query=Paris" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search/mentions - 0-6 credits (request-shaped)

Returns Instagram posts by other accounts that tag an account or @mention it in the caption. Each call runs two searches: the account's Tagged tab (/v1/instagram/tagged, `match_kind` `tag`) and reels whose caption mentions `@handle` (/v1/instagram/search/reels, kept only when the caption carries the @handle or links the profile, `match_kind` `mention` or `link`). The Tagged tab is the one Instagram surface for posts that tag an account, and an account that approves its tags by hand can show older posts there, which is why the caption search runs as well. The account's own posts are left out unless `include_self=true`. Rows are merged newest first and a post found twice appears once. Each row in `data.items` is exactly the row the named search endpoint returns, with its `post` and `computed` blocks, plus `match_kind`. `since` and `until` keep only rows published inside the window. Send `data.next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null when every search has run out. `data.legs` reports each search: its endpoint, status, rows returned and kept, credits and `request_id`. `data.excluded` counts the rows left out (`unmatched`, `self`, `duplicate`, `outside_window`). Each call is one page of each search at its own price: 5 credits for the Tagged page and 1 for the reels page, so at most 6.

**Use when** you want to track who tags or mentions a brand on Instagram, including brands whose Tagged tab is curated; since/until keep rows inside a date window.
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · cache 120 s
**Pricing** Metered, 0-6 credits: each call reads one page of /v1/instagram/tagged (5 credits) and /v1/instagram/search/reels (1 credit), each billed at that endpoint's own price exactly as a direct call is. A page that found nothing or failed costs nothing, and a page served from cache is free. A page is billed when it returned rows, even if none of them carried the mention; data.legs shows each page's charge and data.excluded what was left out.
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 4.8-19 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - The account's username, with or without the @, or its profile URL. · e.g. `myntra`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - data.next_cursor from the previous response, sent back verbatim for the next page.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only posts published on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only posts published on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC); that whole day is included.
- `include_self` (optional, boolean) - When true, also keep posts by the account itself. Default false.

**Response** `Analytics`. Fields not published yet - call it once; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=instagram/search/mentions` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/search/mentions" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=myntra" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search/music - 5 credits (advanced)

Searches Instagram's audio (music) library by keyword. Returns matching tracks, each with artist and title, audio and cover-artwork URLs, duration, and usage metadata. Page through with `cursor`. When the main source is unavailable, page 1 can come from a backup source: about 10 tracks, `song_monetization_info` null, and no `next_cursor`. That page is not cached, so calling again later returns the full page with its cursor.

**Use when** you want to find a specific sound by name; music/trending is the choice when you want whatever is popular right now. **Not for** what is popular right now (instagram/music/trending).
**Cost** cache 21600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** cursor · ≈30/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/30) x 5 credits · typical 2.3-3.2 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search keyword or phrase to find Instagram audio tracks. · e.g. `beyonce`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Use the `next_cursor` from the previous response to fetch the next page.

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ metadata, track }` (inferred from a sample): `metadata` {allow_media_creation_with_music boolean, is_bookmarked boolean, is_trending_in_clips boolean}; `track` {allows_saving boolean, audio_asset_id string, audio_cluster_id string, cover_artwork_thumbnail_uri string, cover_artwork_uri string, dark_message null, display_artist string, duration_in_ms number, fast_start_progressive_download_url string, has_lyrics boolean, highlight_start_times_in_ms number[], id string, is_eligible_for_audio_effects boolean, is_eligible_for_vinyl_sticker boolean, is_explicit boolean, licensed_music_subtype string, progressive_download_url string, reactive_audio_download_url null, sanitized_title null, song_monetization_info string, subtitle string, title string} (+2 more).

Page-level: `data.dropped`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/search/music" \
  --data-urlencode "query=beyonce" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search/popular - 1-13 credits (request-shaped)

Returns popular Instagram posts matching a keyword. Each post includes caption, play count, permalink, thumbnail, and the owner's username. The popular surface itself does not publish like or comment counts, the post date or the duration, so on a plain call `post.engagement.likes`, `.comments`, `.shares`, `post.published_at` and `post.content.duration_seconds` are null. Send `include=engagement` and every row is joined, in the same call, to the per-post lookup that carries them: likes, comments, shares (the paper-plane send count), views, the exact publish time and the duration land on each row. Cost: 1 credit for the page plus 1 credit per row that was filled from a fresh lookup (12 rows max, so 13 credits at most); rows already in cache are filled for free, rows that could not be filled are refunded, and a repeat of the same call within the cache window is 0 credits. Time: a plain call is 2 to 3 seconds; `include=engagement` adds 2 to 9 seconds on a fresh page (the twelve lookups run in parallel and the call waits for the slowest, never more than 12 seconds) and nothing when the rows are already cached. `limit=N` caps the rows and the credits together. The response carries a `hydration` block itemising rows, lookups, cache hits, credits and milliseconds. Accounts that hide their like count keep `likes` null. `post.engagement.saves` is not available on this surface and stays null either way. Page with cursor. Instagram has no popular page for some queries, often place names or rare phrases: those calls return 404 at no charge, so use /v1/instagram/search/reels for the same keyword instead.

**Use when** you want to sample what is popular for a topic; search/reels is the choice when you want a keyword reel feed instead. **Not for** a reel feed (instagram/search/reels) or one specific tag (instagram/search/hashtag).
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit for the page. include=engagement holds 1 credit per row, at most 12 (or `limit`), and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup, so a full page is at most 13 credits; rows served from cache are free, unfilled rows are refunded, and a repeat of the same call within the cache window costs 0. Search pages are cached for 2 minutes and the per-post lookups for 10 minutes.
**Paging** cursor · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 2.1-4.6 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Keyword or topic to find popular Instagram posts. · e.g. `basketball`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Cursor from the previous response to fetch the next page.
- `include` (optional, enum: engagement) - Set to `engagement` (one token only) to fill `post.engagement.likes`, `.comments`, `.shares`, `.views`, `post.published_at` and `post.content.duration_seconds` on every row in this one call. Holds 1 credit per row (at most 12, or `limit`) and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup; rows already in cache and rows that could not be filled are refunded, so the most a call can cost is 1 + rows and the usual bill is lower. Adds 2 to 9 seconds on a fresh page (never more than 12) and nothing when the rows are already cached; read `data.hydration` for the rows, the credits held and kept, and the time.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-12) - Take the top N rows of the page (1 to 12) after the search has run. With `include=engagement` it also caps the extra credits at N: `limit=5&include=engagement` costs at most 6. It is not a page size: `next_cursor` still advances past the full page, so rows beyond N on this page are not returned by the next page.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. (with `include=engagement`) (only when the fallback source serves) |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+17 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, shares, views}; `post.ext` {author_id, ig_play_count}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Never filled: `post.engagement.saves`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.pinned`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.hydration`.

**Next** `instagram/post` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post details. · `instagram/post/stats` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Instagram post stats including the share count. · `instagram/profile` (`handle` ← `data.items[].post.author.username`) - Get Instagram user profile. · `instagram/profile/full` (`handle` ← `data.items[].post.author.username`) - Instagram profile, recent posts, and computed analytics in one call.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/search/popular" \
  --data-urlencode "query=basketball" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search/profiles - 1-25 credits (request-shaped)

Searches Instagram's own account search for a keyword or phrase and returns matching public profiles mapped to the unified Author schema: `id`, `username`, `display_name`, `verified`, `avatar_url`, and the profile `url`, 20 a page with a `cursor` for the next. A search row carries no `bio`, `followers`, `following` or `posts_count` (they are null): fetch /v1/instagram/profile for an account you keep. The plain call has no account country: Instagram does not put that on a search stub. Send `include=about` to join each row to the About-this-account panel for `author.ext.country`, the join month, and the public email and phone the account publishes, 2 extra credits a row filled, default the top 8 (17 credits held), `limit=12` for the page. A row the panel could not fill is refunded. This is not a country filter: a query that surfaces no Korean accounts still returns no Korean accounts after the join. For place-tagged posts, use /v1/instagram/search/location then /v1/instagram/location/posts.

**Use when** you want to find accounts by topic through Instagram's own account search, then call instagram/profile for the bio and follower counts of the ones you keep. **Not for** posts or reels (instagram/search/hashtag, instagram/search/reels), or for accounts, hashtags and places in one payload (instagram/search).
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit for the search page. With `include=about`, 1 plus 2 credits per row filled, held at the top 8 (17) unless you send `limit`, refunded down to the rows that actually received an About-panel leaf.
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 2.2-18 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Keyword or phrase matched against account usernames and display names, as Instagram's own account search does. · e.g. `yoga`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pagination cursor. Pass the `next_cursor` from the previous response to get the next page; treat it as an opaque token.
- `include` (optional, enum: about) - Send `about` to fill `author.ext.country`, join month and public contact from the About panel, 2 extra credits a row filled, never more than 12 rows. A typo is a free 400.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-12) - Cap the rows served, and with `include=about` the credits held. 1 to 12. Default 8 when the token is present so the hold is 17, not 25.

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+9 more (types in the full schema): `author` {external_url, followers, following, posts_count, verified}; `author.ext` {account_created, country, public_email, public_phone}. Never filled: `author.likes_count`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.hydration`.

**Next** `instagram/profile` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - The author's profile: followers, bio and counts. · `instagram/profile/posts` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - The account's latest posts. · `instagram/profile/reels/full` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - Instagram reels with views, likes, comments, and per-reel share counts where available, in one call. · `instagram/profile/posts/full` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - Instagram posts with views, likes, comments, and per-post share counts where available, in one call.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/search/profiles" \
  --data-urlencode "query=yoga" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/search/reels - 1-69 credits (request-shaped)

Searches Instagram for reels matching a keyword query. Returns matching reels with view counts (engagement.views, the play count), like counts, comment counts, and author info, sourced from the Instagram surface that still carries play counts. Each row carries post.ext.author_id (the creator's numeric user id) and post.author.username. `post.ext.author_followers` is null on a plain call, because Instagram stopped sending follower counts in its search payload in August 2026; `include=creator` fills it. Three optional params add what the search itself lacks. Each works alone, and they combine; without them the call is unchanged. `region` (ES, MX, DE, BR, KR, FR, ZA, NG or KE) localises the results. Instagram does not rank search by country, so the market's own name is added to your query (`fitness` becomes `fitness españa`), unless the query already names the market or is already written in the market's own script (Hangul for KR), which Instagram localises by itself. The response reports what ran in `data.region`: `{ requested, method: "localised_query", query_sent }`. `region` favours creators from that market but does not promise that every creator is from it; `country` does. `include=creator` adds each reel's creator card, read from the creator's About this account panel: `post.ext.author_country`, `author_followers`, `author_following`, `author_posts_count`, `author_public_email` and `author_public_phone`, plus the name, avatar and verified flag where the row lacks them. It labels rows and never drops, adds or reorders them. `include=country` adds only `post.ext.author_country`, the same value, read from the creator's panel by `post.ext.author_id` for 1 credit per creator whose country came back, and `include=creator,country` is the same call as `include=creator`. `author_country` is the country the creator declares on that panel, not where the reel was filmed. A null means Instagram does not publish one for that creator, and nothing is guessed. `country` keeps only the reels whose creator declares that market. It adds the creator card, and when `region` is not sent it localises the query for the same market. `data.country` reports `{ requested, kept, dropped_other, dropped_unknown }`: rows from another country, and rows whose creator publishes none, are dropped and counted. Topics about a place, such as travel or eSIMs, are often made by visitors, so the localised query finds fewer local creators there. A phrasing locals use helps (`esim móvil` rather than `esim`), and `country` keeps only the market's creators. `region` and `country` mean what they mean on TikTok search. Only the mechanism of `region` differs: TikTok searches from the market, while Instagram, which ignores where a search comes from, gets a localised query. Price: `region` costs nothing extra. The creator card costs 2 credits per creator looked up. Two reels by one creator are one lookup, a creator that cannot be found is refunded, and a creator looked up in the last 15 minutes is free. Time: `region` adds nothing. The creator card typically adds about 5 to 17 seconds on a fresh page (the lookups run 12 at a time), and little when the creators were looked up in the last 15 minutes. `data.hydration` reports the rows, lookups, cache hits, credits held and kept, and the time. On a `max_pages` walk each creator is looked up once, the report sums every page, and `from_earlier_pages` counts rows filled free from a creator already looked up earlier in the walk. A walk starts another page with the creator card only while at least 30 seconds of its time remain, so a `max_pages` walk with `include=creator` or `country` often stops after its first fresh page with `stopped: "time_budget"`; pages whose creators are cached go further. `data._warnings` carries `creator_partial` when some creators could not be read (they are refunded) and `creator_unavailable` when none could. With `country`, a page where no creator matches is `items: []` with the warning `country_no_match`, and its lookups are still billed. A page left empty only because the creator lookups failed costs nothing. `format=raw` cannot be combined with `include=creator` or `country`; that is a free 400. Note: engagement.shares carries the reel's share count on most rows; it is null where Instagram's search surface omits it, on date-filtered searches, and on pages served while that surface is unavailable. For a share count on every reel, pass a result URL to /v1/instagram/post/stats, or use /v1/instagram/profile/reels/full to get a whole creator's reels with share counts merged in. engagement.saves is null: saves are platform-private. Instagram exposes no numeric save metric on any surface, and it is never fabricated. Result ordering is Instagram's own relevance ranking and is not stable between calls: the same query re-run minutes later can return a different, overlapping set. Rank on engagement.views client-side rather than relying on result order, and deduplicate by post.id across pages. Note on date_posted: filtered searches are served by the only Instagram surface that offers a date filter, and that surface no longer carries play counts, so engagement.views is null when date_posted is set. If you need both a date window and view counts, omit date_posted and filter on published_at yourself. Pagination: forward `pagination.next_cursor` back as `cursor` and keep calling while `pagination.has_more` is true. The walk ends with `has_more: false` and an empty `items` list, charged 0 credits. Two things during a walk are normal and are not the end: a page can come back empty at 0 credits, when every reel on it was already returned earlier in the same walk or when Instagram answers that page with an empty result, and page sizes vary, so keep going while `has_more` is true and do not stop on the first short or empty page. Follow `next_cursor` in preference to requesting page numbers yourself: the cursor carries the reels already delivered, so repeats are dropped and a page with nothing new is not charged, while a bare `page=3` can return reels from an earlier page. A query with no matches returns an empty list rather than an error. A short keyword query such as `esim europa` usually pages with view counts on every page. A long phrase or a question often matches only on a surface that returns one page with view counts, so its later pages come back with engagement.views null. Note that a date-filtered search draws on a much smaller pool: expect roughly 10 reels per page and a walk that ends after a handful of pages, against 30 per page and far greater depth when date_posted is omitted. On a reel also posted to Facebook, `engagement.views` can include its Facebook views: `post.ext.instagram_views` is the Instagram-only figure, the same on every Instagram endpoint, and `post.ext.facebook_views` is the Facebook part when the source reports it.

**Use when** you want it for keyword and topic discovery on Instagram (posts about a brand, phrase or subject), 1 credit a page; search/hashtag is only for a hashtag you already have. Share counts: post/stats. **Not for** a specific hashtag (instagram/search/hashtag), accounts (instagram/search/profiles) or share counts (video posts) at instagram/post/stats.
**Cost** price moves with `country`, `include`, `label` · cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit per page on a plain call or with `region`; `include=creator` or `country` makes it up to 61 (1 plus 2 per creator looked up). `region` costs nothing extra. `include=country` makes it up to 31: 1 extra credit per creator whose declared country came back, refunded for a creator who publishes none or cannot be found. `include=creator` adds 2 credits per creator looked up: it holds 60 extra credits for a full page of 30 and refunds every creator it did not look up or could not find. Two reels by one creator are one lookup, a creator looked up in the last 15 minutes is free, and on a `max_pages` walk each creator is looked up and billed once. `country` runs the same creator lookup, because it needs each creator's declared country, at the same price, charged for every creator looked up, kept or not; `data.hydration.implied_by` says so on the response. `include=creator,country` is priced as `include=creator` alone, because the creator card already carries the country. Relevance against your query (by default, or with relevance=) is free. Adding relevant_to= holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 rows that were newly judged: rows already judged for the same topic are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free. The default labels (sponsored, intent, niche) are free. label=mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection, or label=intent with offer=, holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 posts that were newly judged: posts already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free. With `max_pages`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free). With `seen`, a page's price falls with its share of rows you already received under that id; credits for joined data (`include=`) are never discounted.
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈30/page (observed once) · depth 11 pages (date_posted is set) · price per N items not proven · typical 8.1-19 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search keyword or phrase to find Instagram reels · e.g. `workout routine`
- `date_posted` (optional, enum: last-week | last-month | last-year) - Date posted
- `page` (optional, integer) - The page number to return.
- `region` (optional, enum: ES | MX | DE | BR | KR | FR | ZA | NG | KE) - Two-letter market code (ES, MX, DE, BR, KR, FR, ZA, NG, KE) to localise the results. Instagram does not rank search by country, so the market's own name is appended to your query (`fitness` with `ES` searches `fitness españa`), unless the query already names the market or is already written in the market's own script (Hangul for KR), which Instagram localises by itself. The query actually searched is returned in `data.region.query_sent`. It favours creators from the market but does not promise that every creator is from it; send `country` for that. For a topic about a place, such as eSIMs or travel, a phrasing locals use works better (`esim móvil` rather than `esim`). Same price as a plain call. Only these markets are supported; any other code is refused with the list, at no charge. A typo is a free 400.
- `include` (optional, string) - Send `creator` to add each reel's creator card, read from the creator's About this account panel: `post.ext.author_country`, `author_followers`, `author_following`, `author_posts_count`, `author_public_email` and `author_public_phone`, plus the creator's name, avatar and verified flag where the row lacks them. `author_country` is the country the creator declares there, not where the reel was filmed; it is null when Instagram does not publish one, and nothing is guessed. 2 extra credits per creator looked up; two reels by one creator cost one lookup, a creator that cannot be found is refunded, and a creator looked up in the last 15 minutes is free. Send `country` for the declared country alone (`post.ext.author_country`, the same value): 1 extra credit per creator whose country came back, refunded for a creator who publishes none or cannot be found, and free for a creator looked up in the last 30 days, with no counts or contact. `creator,country` is the same call as `creator`. A typo is a free 400.
- `country` (optional, enum: ES | MX | DE | BR | KR | FR | ZA | NG | KE) - Two-letter market code (ES, MX, DE, BR, KR, FR, ZA, NG, KE) to keep only reels whose creator is based in that market. Costs up to 61 credits a page, not 1: 1 credit plus 2 per creator looked up, kept or not, because the country is read from each creator's own profile (`post.ext.author_country`). It therefore adds the creator card (`include=creator`, reported as `data.hydration.implied_by: "country"`) and, when `region` is not sent, localises the query for the same market. To localise without the lookups, send `region` alone (1 credit). Rows from another country, or whose creator publishes none, are dropped and counted in `data.country` (`kept`, `dropped_other`, `dropped_unknown`); kept rows keep their order. When no row matches, the page is `items: []` with the warning `country_no_match`, and the lookups are still billed. A page left empty only because the creator lookups failed costs nothing. Works with `max_pages`. A typo is a free 400.
- `ai_written_threshold` (optional, string) - Optional, only with label=ai_written and exclude=ai_written. The p (0 to 1) at which exclude=ai_written drops a post. Default 0.95 (level likely). 0.71 also drops possible posts: more AI posts go, and more posts by people with them.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sponsored | mention | intent | niche | quality | ai_style | ai_written | injection; paid: mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection) · `exclude` (engagement_bait | ai_style | ai_written) · `label_evidence` (1) · `brand` · `brand_description` · `offer` · `relevance` (score | filter) · `relevant_to` · `relevance_threshold` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality); `max_pages` (1-5) · `seen` · `min_views` (min 0) · `max_age_days` (1-3650) · `sort_rows` (views) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks)

**Constraints**

- `ai_written_threshold` is a no-op without `label` - sending it alone is a free 400.
- `relevance_threshold`, `relevant_to` are no-ops without `relevance` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `exclude`, `brand`, `brand_description`, `offer`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `include`: at most 2 comma-separated values; each value one of creator | country.
- `label`: at most 8 comma-separated values.
- `exclude`: at most 3 comma-separated values.

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.content.text` | 100% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to author profile picture |
| `post.author.verified` | 100% | Whether the author account is verified |

+33 more (types in the full schema): `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls}; `post.engagement` {comments, views, likes}; `post.ext` {author_id}; `post` {url}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, labels_evidence, language, relevance}; `computed.labels` {ai_style, ai_written, injection, intent, mention, niche} (+14 more). Never filled: `post.engagement.saves`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.country`, `data.dropped`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.hydration`, `data.labels`, `data.region`, `data.relevance`, `data.walk`.
