## GET /v1/instagram/similar - 5-85 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a list of Instagram accounts similar to a given user: the related accounts Instagram surfaces as suggestions. Each account includes username, display name, avatar URL, verification status, and profile URL. Pass either `handle` or `user_id`. Passing `user_id` is faster because no username lookup is needed. This is a suggestion list, so on a plain call the per-account metrics are null on every row: author.followers, author.following, author.posts_count and author.bio. Send `include=profile` and every row is joined, in the same call, to the profile lookup that carries them: exact follower and following counts plus the bio land on each row. `author.posts_count` lands only on a row the lookup's backup source answered, so it is null on most rows; `GET /v1/instagram/profile` returns the lifetime post count for any single account. Cost: 5 credits for the list plus 1 credit per row filled from a fresh lookup; rows already in cache are free, unfilled rows are refunded, and a repeat within the cache window is 0. With `include=profile` the list is its top 20 accounts unless you pass `limit` (1 to 80), so the default hydrated call is at most 25 credits (the same as `limit=20&include=profile`) and `limit=80&include=profile`, the full roster, is at most 85. Time: a plain call is 2 to 3 seconds; with `include=profile` allow 3 to 6 seconds more for 20 rows (the lookups run in parallel and the call waits for the slowest, never more than 12 seconds) and about four times that for all 80, which run as four waves of 24. The response carries a `hydration` block itemising rows, lookups, cache hits, credits and milliseconds. author.likes_count stays null: Instagram publishes no account-level like total. The list is a single fixed window: it is not paginated and returns no cursor.

**Use when** you want to find accounts comparable to one you already know; it returns a single fixed list and cannot be paged.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits for the list. include=profile holds 1 credit per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup; the hydrated list is its top 20 accounts by default (at most 25 credits) and `limit=80` buys the full roster (at most 85). Rows served from cache are free, unfilled rows are refunded, and a repeat within the cache window costs 0. The list and the per-account lookups are cached for 15 minutes.
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username without the @ symbol. · e.g. `mrbeast`
- `user_id` (optional, string) - Instagram numeric user ID. Use this for faster responses.
- `include` (optional, enum: profile) - Set to `profile` (one token only) to fill `author.followers`, `author.following` and `author.bio` on every row in this one call, plus `author.posts_count` where the lookup has an exact total. The hydrated list is its top 20 accounts unless you pass `limit` (1 to 80). Holds 1 credit per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup; rows already in cache and rows that could not be filled are refunded, so the most a call can cost is 5 + rows (25 by default, 85 with `limit=80`) and the usual bill is lower. Adds 3 to 6 seconds for 20 rows (never more than 12) and about four times that for 80, and nothing when the accounts are already cached; read `data.hydration` for the rows, the credits held and kept, and the time.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-80) - Take the top N accounts of the list (1 to 80). With `include=profile` the list defaults to its top 20 (at most 25 credits) and `limit` caps both the rows and the extra credits: `limit=80&include=profile` buys the full roster for at most 85 credits. Without `include=profile` the full list is returned unless you cap it.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `handle`, `user_id`.

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description (with `include=profile`) |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+5 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, posts_count, verified, private}. Never filled: `author.likes_count`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.hydration`.

**Next** `instagram/profile` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - Get Instagram user profile. · `instagram/engagement` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - Get Instagram engagement statistics. · `instagram/profile/full` (`handle` ← `data.items[].author.username`) - Instagram profile, recent posts, and computed analytics in one call.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/similar" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=mrbeast" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/instagram/stories - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns the active stories currently in a user's story tray. Each story includes its id, media URLs (image or video), thumbnail, duration, capture time, and the author. Pass either `handle` or `user_id`. Passing `user_id` is faster because no username lookup is needed. A public account with no active stories returns an empty list at no charge, not an error; a private account returns 404. Stories carry no public caption and no public like, comment, or view count: Instagram shows story engagement only to the account owner, and it is never fabricated here.

**Use when** you want to check an account's current story tray; an account with nothing live returns an empty list rather than an error.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Instagram username without the @ symbol. · e.g. `instagram`
- `user_id` (optional, string) - Instagram numeric user ID. Use this for faster responses.
- `safe_url` (optional, boolean) - Optional and usually ignored: most responses carry ordinary media URLs whether or not you send it. Same price either way.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `handle`, `user_id`.

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+10 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.ext` {media_type string, published_at_epoch number, coauthors array}. Never filled: `post.content.text`, `post.engagement.comments`, `post.engagement.likes`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.engagement.views`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.pinned`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Page-level: `data.dropped`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/stories" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=instagram" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

Returns the downloadable media for one specific story: the full-resolution image or video URLs and the story's metadata. Pass the `user_id` of the story's author and the `story_id` of the individual story (get story ids from the Instagram stories endpoint).

## GET /v1/instagram/tagged - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns a paginated list of the posts that tag an Instagram user. Each post includes shortcode, URL, caption, media URLs, engagement counts, and the author. Pass either `handle` or `user_id`, and page through with `cursor`. Note: post.author.display_name is usually null on this endpoint, because the Instagram surface behind it withholds creator display names; it carries the real name on the calls a second source answers. Join on post.author.username, or pass it to /v1/instagram/profile?handle= for the name.

This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).
- `until` (optional, string) - Only rows published on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. Newer rows are left off each page and the walk does not stop, so older pages follow. A row with no date is kept. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#incremental-sync-since-stop_at_id).

## GET /v1/instagram/user/embed - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the embed for a public Instagram profile. `author.ext.embed_html` is Instagram's own embed code for the profile (a `blockquote` plus the `embed.js` script tag), ready to paste into a page on your site, where it renders the profile card with its latest posts. `author.ext.embed_url` is the address of the frame that script loads (`https://www.instagram.com/<username>/embed/`), for placing the frame yourself. The response also carries the profile the embed shows: username, display name, picture, verification, exact follower count, post count and the account id. The embed does not show the bio or the following count, so those are null; call /v1/instagram/profile for them. Private accounts, accounts that do not allow embeds and handles that do not exist have no embed: they return 404 at no charge, and Instagram's page does not say which of the three it is.

**Use when** you want to display a profile on your site. Private accounts, accounts that do not allow embeds and handles that do not exist return 404 at no charge; profile has the bio and following.
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - Instagram username without the @ symbol · e.g. `instagram`

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |
| `author.followers` | Follower or subscriber count as an integer. |

+10 more (types in the full schema): `author` {posts_count, verified, private}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `author.ext` {embed_html, embed_url}. Never filled: `author.bio`, `author.following`, `author.joined_at`, `author.likes_count`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/user/embed" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=instagram" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
